bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: =陳紀七=

translations.literal: Chen Records, Part Seven
translations.idiomatic: Chen Records, Part Seven

sentences.zh: 起強圉作噩，盡屠維大淵獻，凡三年。

translations.literal: From Qiangyu Zuo'e through Tuwei Dayuanxian; three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Qiangyu Zuo'e through Tuwei Dayuanxian—three years in all.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，乙亥朔，齊太子恆即皇帝位，生八年矣；

translations.literal: 1. In spring, the first month, on the first day of the month (yihai), the Qi crown prince Heng ascended the imperial throne; he was eight years old;
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, on the first day of the first month (yihai), Qi crown prince Heng took the throne; he was eight years old.

sentences.zh: 改元承光，大赦。

translations.literal: The era name was changed to Chengguang, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: The era was renamed Chengguang and a general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 尊齊主為太上皇帝，皇太后為太皇太后，皇后為太上皇后。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler was honored as Retired Emperor, the empress dowager as Grand Empress Dowager, and the empress as Retired Empress.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi emperor was elevated to Retired Emperor, his mother to Grand Empress Dowager, and his consort to Retired Empress.

sentences.zh: 以廣寧王孝珩為太宰。

translations.literal: Prince Guangning Xiaoxian was appointed Grand Steward.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Guangning Xiaoxian was made Grand Steward.

sentences.zh: 司徒莫多婁敬顯、領軍大將軍尉相願謀伏兵千秋門，斬高阿那肱，立廣寧王孝珩。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Moduolou Jingxian and Commander-in-Chief Wei Xiangyuan plotted to set an ambush at Qianqiu Gate, kill Gao Anagong, and install Prince Guangning Xiaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Education Moduolou Jingxian and Commander-in-Chief Wei Xiangyuan planned an ambush at Qianqiu Gate to kill Gao Anagong and put Prince Guangning Xiaoxian on the throne.

sentences.zh: 會阿那肱自它路入朝，不果。

translations.literal: But Anagong entered court by another route, and the plan failed.
translations.idiomatic: Anagong came to court by another route, however, and the plot came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 孝珩求拒周師，謂阿那肱等曰：「朝廷不賜遣擊賊，豈不畏孝珩反邪？

translations.literal: Xiaoxian asked to resist the Zhou army and said to Anagong and the others: "If the court will not send me to strike the enemy, are you not afraid Xiaoxian will rebel?
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxian asked to be sent against the Zhou forces and told Anagong and the others, "If the court will not let me attack the enemy, are you not afraid I might rebel?

sentences.zh: 孝珩若破宇文邕，遂至長安，反亦何預國家事！

translations.literal: If Xiaoxian should defeat Yuwen Yong and even reach Chang'an, how would rebellion concern the state's affairs!
translations.idiomatic: If I break Yuwen Yong and even reach Chang'an, what would that have to do with the state's affairs!

sentences.zh: 以今日之急，猶如此猜忌邪！」

translations.literal: At today's crisis, you still harbor such suspicion!"
translations.idiomatic: At a crisis like today's, you still treat me with such suspicion!"

sentences.zh: 高、韓恐其為變，出孝珩為滄州刺史。

translations.literal: Gao and Han, fearing he might cause trouble, sent Xiaoxian out as governor of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao and Han, fearing he might make trouble, posted Xiaoxian to Cangzhou as governor.

sentences.zh: 相願拔佩刀斫柱，歎曰：「大事去矣，知復何言！」

translations.literal: Xiangyuan drew his belt sword and hacked a pillar, sighing: "The great affair is lost—what more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyuan drew his sword and struck a pillar, crying, "The great cause is lost—what more is there to say!"

sentences.zh: 齊主使長樂王尉世辯，帥千餘騎覘周師，出滏口，登高阜西望，遙見群烏飛起，謂是西軍旗幟，即馳還；

translations.literal: The Qi ruler sent Prince Changle Wei Shibian to lead more than a thousand horsemen to reconnoiter the Zhou army; leaving Fukou, he climbed a high mound and looked west, and from afar saw a flock of birds rise and took them for Western Army banners, and at once galloped back;
translations.idiomatic: The Qi emperor sent Prince Changle Wei Shibian with more than a thousand horsemen to scout the Zhou army. Leaving Fukou, he climbed a height and looked west; when he saw birds rise in the distance he took them for Zhou banners and galloped back at once.

sentences.zh: 比至紫陌橋，不敢回顧。

translations.literal: By the time he reached Zimo Bridge he dared not look back.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Zimo Bridge he did not dare look behind him.

sentences.zh: 世辯，粲之子也。

translations.literal: Shibian was the son of Can.
translations.idiomatic: Shibian was a son of Wei Can.

sentences.zh: 於是黃門侍郎顏之推、中書侍郎薛道衡、侍中陳德信等勸上皇往河外募兵，更為經略；

translations.literal: Thereupon Attendant Gentleman Yan Zhitui, Secretariat Gentleman Xue Daoheng, Palace Attendant Chen Dexin, and others urged the Retired Emperor to go beyond the Yellow River to raise troops and plan anew;
translations.idiomatic: Then Attendant Gentleman Yan Zhitui, Secretariat Gentleman Xue Daoheng, Palace Attendant Chen Dexin, and others urged the Retired Emperor to cross the Yellow River and raise troops for a fresh strategy.

sentences.zh: 若不濟，南投陳國。

translations.literal: If that did not succeed, they would flee south to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: If that failed, they would flee south to Chen.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: He followed their advice.
translations.idiomatic: He agreed.

sentences.zh: 道衡，孝通之子也。

translations.literal: Daoheng was the son of Xiaotong.
translations.idiomatic: Daoheng was a son of Xue Xiaotong.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，太皇太后、太上皇后自鄴先趣濟州；

translations.literal: On dingchou the Grand Empress Dowager and Retired Empress left Ye first and hurried to Jizhou;
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou the Grand Empress Dowager and Retired Empress left Ye ahead of the others and pressed on to Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 癸未，幼主亦自鄴東行。

translations.literal: On guiwei the young emperor also set out east from Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei the young emperor too departed Ye heading east.

sentences.zh: 己丑，周師至紫陌橋。

translations.literal: On jichou the Zhou army reached Zimo Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou the Zhou army reached Zimo Bridge.

sentences.zh: 2辛卯，上祭北郊。

translations.literal: 2. On xinmao the emperor sacrificed at the Northern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: 2. On xinmao the Chen emperor sacrificed at the Northern Suburb.

sentences.zh: 3壬辰，周師至鄴城下；

translations.literal: 3. On renchen the Zhou army came below the walls of Ye;
translations.idiomatic: 3. On renchen the Zhou army arrived beneath the walls of Ye.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，圍之，燒城西門。

translations.literal: On guisi they besieged it and burned the western gate.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi they laid siege and set fire to the western gate.

sentences.zh: 齊人出戰，周師奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: The Qi forces came out to fight; the Zhou army struck hard and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi came out to fight; the Zhou army struck fiercely and routed them.

sentences.zh: 齊上皇從百騎東走，使武衛大將軍慕容三藏守鄴宮。

translations.literal: The Qi Retired Emperor fled east with a hundred horsemen and left Martial Guard General Murong Sanzang to hold the Ye palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi Retired Emperor fled east with a hundred riders and left Martial Guard General Murong Sanzang to defend the Ye palace.

sentences.zh: 周師入鄴，齊王、公以下皆降。

translations.literal: The Zhou army entered Ye; Qi princes, dukes, and all below submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou army entered Ye, and Qi princes, dukes, and officials down the ranks all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 三藏猶拒戰，周主引見，禮之，拜儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: Sanzang still resisted; the Zhou ruler summoned and honored him, appointing him General of the Same Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Sanzang still fought on; the Zhou emperor received him with honor and made him General of the Same Rites.

sentences.zh: 三藏，紹宗之子也。

translations.literal: Sanzang was the son of Shaozong.
translations.idiomatic: Sanzang was a son of Murong Shaozong.

sentences.zh: 領軍大將軍漁陽鮮于世榮，齊高祖舊將也。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Yuyang Yu Shirong was an old general of Qi Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-Chief Yu Shirong of Yuyang was a veteran of Qi Gaozu's reign.

sentences.zh: 周主先以馬腦酒鐘遺之，世榮得即碎之。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler had first sent him an agate wine goblet; Shirong smashed it as soon as he received it.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor had earlier sent him an agate wine vessel; Shirong smashed it the moment it reached him.

sentences.zh: 周師入鄴，世榮在三台前鳴鼓不輟，周人執之；

translations.literal: When the Zhou army entered Ye, Shirong beat drums without cease before the Three Terraces; the Zhou seized him;
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou entered Ye, Shirong kept beating drums before the Three Terraces until the Zhou seized him.

sentences.zh: 世榮不屈，乃殺之。

translations.literal: Shirong would not submit, and they killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shirong would not yield, so they put him to death.

sentences.zh: 周主執莫多婁敬顯，數之曰：「汝有死罪三：前自晉陽走鄴，攜妾棄母，不孝也；

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler seized Moduolou Jingxian and reckoned his crimes, saying: "You have three capital offenses: formerly you fled from Jinyang to Ye, taking a concubine and abandoning your mother—unfilial;
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor seized Moduolou Jingxian and listed his crimes: "You deserve death three times over: you fled Jinyang for Ye, taking a concubine and leaving your mother behind—that is unfilial;

sentences.zh: 外為偽朝戮力，內實通啟於朕，不忠也；

translations.literal: outwardly you toiled for the false dynasty, inwardly you secretly informed me—disloyal;
translations.idiomatic: outwardly you served the false dynasty, inwardly you opened letters to me—that is disloyal;

sentences.zh: 送款之後，猶持兩端，不信也。

translations.literal: after you pledged allegiance you still wavered between two sides—untrustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: after you submitted you still played both sides—that is faithless.

sentences.zh: 用心如此，不死何待！」

translations.literal: With a heart like this, why should you not die!"
translations.idiomatic: With a heart like that, why should you live!"

sentences.zh: 遂斬之。

translations.literal: He was beheaded at once.
translations.idiomatic: He was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 使將軍尉遲勤追齊主。

translations.literal: He sent General Yuchi Qin in pursuit of the Qi ruler.
translations.idiomatic: He sent General Yuchi Qin to pursue the Qi emperor.

sentences.zh: 甲午，周主入鄴。

translations.literal: On jiawu the Zhou ruler entered Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu the Zhou emperor entered Ye.

sentences.zh: 齊國子博士長樂熊安生，博通《五經》，聞周主入鄴，遽令掃門。

translations.literal: Qi National University Erudite Xiong Ansheng of Changle, thoroughly versed in the Five Classics, on hearing the Zhou ruler had entered Ye, at once ordered his gate swept.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Ansheng of Changle, a Qi National University erudite thoroughly versed in the Five Classics, heard the Zhou emperor had entered Ye and immediately ordered his gate swept clean.

sentences.zh: 家人怪而問之，安生曰：「周帝重道尊儒，必將見我。」

translations.literal: His household wondered and asked why; Ansheng said: "The Zhou emperor values the Way and honors Confucian learning—he is sure to visit me."
translations.idiomatic: His family wondered and asked why; Ansheng said, "The Zhou emperor values the Way and honors Confucian learning—he is sure to call on me."

sentences.zh: 俄而周主幸其家，不聽拜，親執其手，引與同坐；

translations.literal: Before long the Zhou ruler visited his home, would not allow him to bow, personally took his hand, and drew him to sit together;
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Zhou emperor came to his house, forbade him to bow, took his hand himself, and seated him beside him.

sentences.zh: 賞賜甚厚，給安車駟馬以自隨。

translations.literal: rewards were very generous, and a comfort carriage with a four-horse team was given for his use.
translations.idiomatic: He lavished gifts on him and gave him a comfort carriage with a four-horse team to travel at his side.

sentences.zh: 又遣小司馬唐道和就中書侍郎李德林宅宣旨慰諭，曰：「平齊之利，唯在於爾。」

translations.literal: He also sent Junior Marshal Tang Daohe to the residence of Secretariat Gentleman Li Delin to proclaim the imperial will and comfort him, saying: "The profit of pacifying Qi lies in you alone."
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Junior Marshal Tang Daohe to Secretariat Gentleman Li Delin's house with an imperial message of reassurance, saying, "The gain from pacifying Qi rests on you alone."

sentences.zh: 引入宮，使內史宇文昂訪問齊朝風俗政教，人物善惡。

translations.literal: Delin was brought into the palace, and Palace Secretary Yuwen Ang was sent to inquire about Qi customs, government, and teaching, and the good and bad among its people.
translations.idiomatic: Delin was brought to the palace, and Palace Secretary Yuwen Ang was sent to question him on Qi customs, government, and the worth of its leading men.

sentences.zh: 即留內省，三宿乃歸。

translations.literal: He was kept in the inner offices three nights before returning home.
translations.idiomatic: He was kept in the inner offices for three nights before he went home.

sentences.zh: 乙未，齊上皇渡河入濟州。

translations.literal: On yiwei the Qi Retired Emperor crossed the river and entered Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei the Qi Retired Emperor crossed the Yellow River and entered Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 是日，幼主禪位於大丞相任城王湝。

translations.literal: That same day the young emperor abdicated in favor of Grand Chancellor Prince Rencheng Hu.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the young emperor abdicated in favor of Grand Chancellor Prince Rencheng Hu.

sentences.zh: 又為湝詔：尊上皇為無上皇，幼主為宋國天王。

translations.literal: An edict was also issued for Hu: the Retired Emperor was honored as Supreme Retired Emperor, and the young emperor as King of the Song State.
translations.idiomatic: Hu also issued an edict honoring the Retired Emperor as Supreme Retired Emperor and the young emperor as King of Song.

sentences.zh: 令侍中斛律孝卿送禪文及璽紱於瀛州，孝卿即詣鄴。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Hulu Xiaqing was ordered to deliver the abdication document and imperial seal and cord to Yingzhou; Xiaqing went straight to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Palace Attendant Hulu Xiaqing to take the abdication text and the imperial seal and cord to Yingzhou, but Xiaqing went straight to Ye instead.

sentences.zh: 周主詔：「去年大赦所未及之處，皆從赦例。」

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler decreed: "Places not covered by last year's general amnesty shall all follow the amnesty precedent."
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor decreed, "All places not covered by last year's general amnesty shall be included under the amnesty."

sentences.zh: 齊洛州刺史獨孤永業，有甲士三萬，聞晉州敗，請出兵擊周，奏寢不報；

translations.literal: Qi Governor of Luozhou Dugu Yongye had thirty thousand armored troops; hearing of Jinzhou's defeat, he asked to march out and strike Zhou, but his memorial slept without reply;
translations.idiomatic: Qi governor of Luozhou Dugu Yongye had thirty thousand armored troops; when he heard Jinzhou had fallen he asked to march out against Zhou, but his memorial went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 永業憤慨。

translations.literal: Yongye was indignant.
translations.idiomatic: Yongye was furious.

sentences.zh: 又聞并州陷，乃遣子須達請降於周，周以永業為上柱國，封應公。

translations.literal: Hearing also that Bingzhou had fallen, he sent his son Xuda to request surrender to Zhou; Zhou made Yongye Supreme Pillar of State and enfeoffed him as Duke of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: When he also heard Bingzhou had fallen he sent his son Xuda to surrender to Zhou; Zhou made Yongye Supreme Pillar of State and enfeoffed him as Duke of Ying.

sentences.zh: 丙申，周以越王盛為相州總管。

translations.literal: On bingshen Zhou appointed Prince Yue Sheng as overall commander of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Zhou appointed Prince Yue Sheng overall commander of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 齊上皇留胡太后於濟州，使高阿那肱守濟州關，覘候周師，自與穆後、馮淑妃、幼主、韓長鸞、鄧長顒等數十人奔青州。

translations.literal: The Qi Retired Emperor left Empress Dowager Hu at Jizhou, set Gao Anagong to hold the Jizhou pass and watch the Zhou army, and himself with Consort Mu, Lady Feng, the young emperor, Han Changluan, Deng Changyan, and several dozen others fled to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi Retired Emperor left Empress Dowager Hu at Jizhou, put Gao Anagong in charge of the Jizhou pass to watch the Zhou army, and fled to Qingzhou with Consort Mu, Lady Feng, the young emperor, Han Changluan, Deng Changyan, and several dozen others.

sentences.zh: 使內參田鵬鸞西出，參伺動靜；

translations.literal: He sent Inner Attendant Tian Pengluan west to observe movements;
translations.idiomatic: He sent Inner Attendant Tian Pengluan west to scout the situation.

sentences.zh: 周師獲之，問齊主何在，紿云：「已去，計當出境。」

translations.literal: the Zhou army captured him and asked where the Qi ruler was; he deceived them, saying: "He has already gone; he should be crossing the border by now."
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou army seized him and asked where the Qi emperor was; he lied, "He has already gone—I expect he is crossing the border by now."

sentences.zh: 周人疑其不信，捶之。

translations.literal: The Zhou men doubted him and beat him.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou doubted him and beat him.

sentences.zh: 每折一支，辭色愈厲，竟折四支而死。

translations.literal: Each time a limb was broken his words and bearing grew fiercer; in the end four limbs were broken and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Each time they broke a limb his tone grew fiercer; they broke all four limbs and he died.

sentences.zh: 上皇至青州，即欲入陳。

translations.literal: When the Retired Emperor reached Qingzhou he at once wished to enter Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When the Retired Emperor reached Qingzhou he at once meant to flee into Chen.

sentences.zh: 而高阿那肱密召周師，約生致齊主，屢啟云：「周師尚遠，已令燒斷橋路。」

translations.literal: But Gao Anagong secretly summoned the Zhou army, agreeing to deliver the Qi ruler alive, and repeatedly reported: "The Zhou army is still far off; I have already ordered the bridges burned and the roads cut."
translations.idiomatic: But Gao Anagong secretly summoned the Zhou army, promising to take the Qi emperor alive, and repeatedly reported, "The Zhou army is still far away; I have already had the bridges burned and the roads cut."

sentences.zh: 上皇由是淹留自寬。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor therefore lingered and took ease.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor therefore lingered and took comfort.

sentences.zh: 周師至關，阿那肱即降之。

translations.literal: When the Zhou army reached the pass, Anagong at once surrendered to them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou army reached the pass, Anagong surrendered at once.

sentences.zh: 周師奄至青州，上皇囊金，繫於鞍後，與後、妃、幼主等十餘騎南走。

translations.literal: The Zhou army suddenly reached Qingzhou; the Retired Emperor bagged gold and tied it behind his saddle, and with the empress, consorts, the young emperor, and more than ten riders fled south.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou army suddenly appeared at Qingzhou; the Retired Emperor stuffed gold into a bag tied behind his saddle and fled south with the empress, consorts, the young emperor, and a dozen riders.

sentences.zh: 己亥，至南鄧村。

translations.literal: On jihai they reached Nandeng Village.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai they reached Nandeng Village.

sentences.zh: 尉遲勤追及，盡擒之，並胡太后送鄴。

translations.literal: Yuchi Qin overtook them, seized them all, and sent them with Empress Dowager Hu to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Qin caught up, seized them all, and sent them with Empress Dowager Hu to Ye.

sentences.zh: 庚子，周主詔：「故斛律光、崔季舒等，宜追加贈謚，並為改葬，子孫各隨廕敘錄。

translations.literal: On gengzi the Zhou ruler decreed: "The late Hulu Guang, Cui Jishu, and others should receive posthumous titles and reburial, and their descendants should each be entered on the registers according to inherited privilege.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the Zhou emperor decreed, "The late Hulu Guang, Cui Jishu, and others shall receive posthumous honors and reburial, and their descendants shall be entered on the registers according to inherited privilege.

sentences.zh: 家口田宅沒官者，並還之。」

translations.literal: Households, fields, and dwellings confiscated by the state shall all be returned."
translations.idiomatic: Households, fields, and dwellings seized by the state shall all be restored."

sentences.zh: 周主指斛律光名曰：「此人在，朕安得至鄴！」

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler pointed to Hulu Guang's name and said: "Had this man been alive, how could I have reached Ye!"
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor pointed to Hulu Guang's name and said, "Had this man lived, how could I have reached Ye!"

sentences.zh: 辛丑，詔：「齊之東山、南園、三台，並可毀撤。

translations.literal: On xinchou he decreed: "Qi's Eastern Hill, Southern Park, and Three Terraces may all be torn down.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou he decreed, "Qi's Eastern Hill, Southern Park, and Three Terraces shall all be demolished.

sentences.zh: 瓦木諸物，可用者悉以賜民。

translations.literal: Tiles, timber, and all usable materials shall be given entirely to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Tiles, timber, and whatever else can be used shall be given to the people.

sentences.zh: 山園之田，各還其主。」

translations.literal: Fields of hill parks shall each be returned to their owners."
translations.idiomatic: The fields of the hill parks shall be returned to their owners."

sentences.zh: 4二月，壬午，上耕藉田。

translations.literal: 4. In the second month, on renwu, the emperor plowed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: 4. In the second month, on renwu, the Chen emperor plowed the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 5丙午，周主宴從官將士於齊太極殿，頒賞有差。

translations.literal: 5. On bingwu the Zhou ruler feasted accompanying officials and generals in Qi's Hall of Supreme Pole and distributed rewards in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: 5. On bingwu the Zhou emperor feasted his officials and generals in Qi's Hall of Supreme Pole and gave rewards in varying measure.

sentences.zh: 丁未，高緯至鄴，周主降價，以賓禮見之。

translations.literal: On dingwei Gao Wei reached Ye; the Zhou ruler came down the steps and received him with guest ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Gao Wei arrived at Ye; the Zhou emperor came down to meet him with the ceremony due a guest.

sentences.zh: 齊廣寧王孝珩至滄州，以五千人會任城王湝於信都，共謀匡復，召募得四萬餘人。

translations.literal: Qi Prince Guangning Xiaoxian reached Cangzhou and with five thousand men joined Prince Rencheng Hu at Xindu; together they plotted restoration and raised more than forty thousand recruits.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Prince Guangning Xiaoxian reached Cangzhou and joined Prince Rencheng Hu at Xindu with five thousand men; together they plotted to restore Qi and raised more than forty thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 周主使齊王憲、柱國楊堅擊之。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler sent Prince Qi Xian and Pillar of State Yang Jian to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor sent Prince Qi Xian and Pillar of State Yang Jian against them.

sentences.zh: 令高緯為手書招湝不從。

translations.literal: Gao Wei was made to write a personal letter summoning Hu, but Hu would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Wei was made to write a personal summons to Hu, but Hu refused.

sentences.zh: 憲軍至趙州，湝遣二諜覘之，候騎執以白憲。

translations.literal: When Xian's army reached Zhao Prefecture, Hu sent two spies to observe them; outriders seized them and reported to Xian.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian's army reached Zhao Prefecture, Hu sent two spies to scout it; outriders seized them and reported to Xian.

sentences.zh: 憲集齊舊將，遍示之，謂曰：「吾所爭者大，不在汝曹。

translations.literal: Xian gathered Qi's former generals, showed the spies to them all, and said: "What I contend for is great; it is not with you people.
translations.idiomatic: Xian assembled Qi's former generals, showed the spies to them all, and said, "The stake I fight for is great; it is not with you.

sentences.zh: 今縱汝還，仍充吾使。」

translations.literal: Today I release you to return—you shall still serve as my envoys."
translations.idiomatic: Today I release you to go back—you shall still serve as my messengers."

sentences.zh: 乃與湝書曰：「足下諜者為候騎所拘，軍中情實，具諸執事。

translations.literal: He then wrote to Hu: "Your spies were detained by outriders; the true state of the army has been laid out fully to those in charge.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote to Hu, "Your spies were seized by outriders; the true state of my army has been laid out in full to your officers.

sentences.zh: 戰非上計，無待卜疑；

translations.literal: Battle is not the superior plan—no need to wait on divination;
translations.idiomatic: Fighting is not the best plan—no need to consult the oracle;

sentences.zh: 守乃下策，或未相許。

translations.literal: holding out is the inferior plan, and perhaps you will not agree to that either.
translations.idiomatic: holding out is the lesser plan, and perhaps you will not agree to that either.

sentences.zh: 已勒諸軍分道並進，相望非遠，憑軾有期。

translations.literal: I have already ordered the armies to advance by separate routes in concert; we are not far from sight of one another—leaning on the chariot rail, our meeting is near.
translations.idiomatic: I have already ordered the armies to advance on separate routes; we are not far apart, and meeting face to face is near.

sentences.zh: 『不俟終日』，所望知機也！」

translations.literal: Not waiting for the day's end'—what I hope is that you know the moment!"
translations.idiomatic: Not waiting for the day's end"—I hope you will know when to act!"

sentences.zh: 憲至信都，湝陳於城南以拒之。

translations.literal: When Xian reached Xindu, Hu drew up his battle line south of the city to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian reached Xindu, Hu drew up his line south of the city to meet him.

sentences.zh: 湝所署領軍尉相願詐出略陳，遂以眾降。

translations.literal: Hu's appointed Commander-in-Chief Wei Xiangyuan pretended to go out and skirmish with the line, then led his troops in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Hu's appointed commander-in-chief Wei Xiangyuan pretended to ride out and skirmish, then surrendered with his troops.

sentences.zh: 相願，湝心腹也，眾皆駭懼。

translations.literal: Xiangyuan was Hu's closest confidant, and all the troops were struck with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyuan was Hu's closest confidant, and the whole army was terrified.

sentences.zh: 湝殺相願妻子。

translations.literal: Hu killed Xiangyuan's wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Hu had Xiangyuan's wife and children killed.

sentences.zh: 明日，復戰，憲擊破之，俘斬三萬人，執湝及廣寧王孝珩。

translations.literal: The next day they fought again; Xian routed them, capturing and killing thirty thousand, and seized Hu and Prince Guangning Xiaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they fought again; Xian routed them, killed or captured thirty thousand, and seized Hu and Prince Guangning Xiaoxian.

sentences.zh: 憲謂湝曰：「任城王何苦至此？」

translations.literal: Xian said to Hu: "Prince Rencheng, why bring yourself to such distress?"
translations.idiomatic: Xian said to Hu, "Prince Rencheng, why did you have to come to this?"

sentences.zh: 湝曰：「下官神武皇帝之子，兄弟十五人，幸而獨存。

translations.literal: Hu said: "Your humble servant is a son of Emperor Shenwu; of fifteen brothers I alone survive by fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Hu said, "I am a son of Emperor Shenwu; of fifteen brothers I alone survive by fortune.

sentences.zh: 逢宗社顛覆，今日得死，無愧墳陵。」

translations.literal: When the altars were overturned, to die today is to be without shame before the tombs."
translations.idiomatic: When the state fell, to die today is to face the tombs without shame."

sentences.zh: 憲壯之，命歸其妻子。

translations.literal: Xian admired his spirit and ordered Xiangyuan's wife and children returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xian admired his spirit and had Xiangyuan's wife and children restored to him.

sentences.zh: 又親為孝珩洗瘡傅藥，禮遇甚厚。

translations.literal: He also personally washed Xiaoxian's sores and applied medicine, treating him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He also washed Xiaoxian's sores and applied medicine himself, treating him with exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 孝珩歎曰：「自神武皇帝以外，吾諸父兄弟，無一人至四十者，命也。

translations.literal: Xiaoxian sighed: "Apart from Emperor Shenwu, not one of my uncles and brothers reached forty—such is fate.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxian sighed, "Apart from Emperor Shenwu, not one of my uncles and brothers lived to forty—that is fate.

sentences.zh: 嗣君無獨見之明，宰相非柱石之寄，恨不得握兵符，受斧鉞，展我心力耳！」

translations.literal: The heir lacked vision of his own, the chancellor was no pillar of trust—I only regret I could not grasp the tally and receive the axe and halberd to expend my heart's strength!"
translations.idiomatic: The heir had no vision of his own, the chancellor was no pillar of the state—I only wish I could have held the command tally and taken the axe to give my full strength!"

sentences.zh: 齊王憲善用兵，多謀略，得將士心。

translations.literal: Prince Qi Xian was skilled in warfare, full of stratagems, and won the hearts of generals and troops.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qi Xian was skilled in war, full of stratagems, and won the hearts of officers and men.

sentences.zh: 齊人憚其威聲，多望風沮潰。

translations.literal: Qi men feared his prestige and many collapsed at the mere rumor of his approach.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi feared his reputation, and many collapsed at the mere rumor of his approach.

sentences.zh: 芻牧不擾，軍無私焉。

translations.literal: Fodder and herds were not disturbed; the army took nothing for private gain.
translations.idiomatic: He did not disturb fodder or herds, and his army took nothing for private gain.

sentences.zh: 周主以齊降將封輔相為北朔州總管。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler appointed the Qi surrendering general Feng Fuxiang as overall commander of North Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor appointed the Qi defector Feng Fuxiang overall commander of North Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 北朔州，齊之重鎮，士卒驍勇。

translations.literal: North Shuozhou was a great fortress of Qi; its troops were fierce and brave.
translations.idiomatic: North Shuozhou was a key Qi stronghold, and its troops were fierce.

sentences.zh: 前長史趙穆等謀執輔相迎任城王湝於瀛州，不果，乃迎定州刺史范陽王紹義。

translations.literal: Former Chief Clerk Zhao Mu and others plotted to seize Fuxiang and welcome Prince Rencheng Hu at Yingzhou; it failed, and they welcomed Prince Fanyang Shaoyi, governor of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Former chief clerk Zhao Mu and others plotted to seize Fuxiang and welcome Prince Rencheng Hu at Yingzhou; when that failed they welcomed Prince Fanyang Shaoyi, governor of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 紹義至馬邑，自肆州以北二百八十餘城皆應之。

translations.literal: When Shaoyi reached Mayi, more than two hundred and eighty cities from Sizhou north all responded to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoyi reached Mayi, more than two hundred and eighty cities from Sizhou north rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 紹義與靈州刺史袁洪猛引兵南出，欲取并州。

translations.literal: Shaoyi and Governor of Lingzhou Yuan Hongmeng led troops south, intending to take Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyi and Lingzhou governor Yuan Hongmeng marched south intending to take Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 至新興，而肆州已為周守，前隊二儀同以所部降周。

translations.literal: When they reached Xinxing, Sizhou was already held by Zhou; two Generals of the Same Rites in the vanguard surrendered their commands to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Xinxing they found Sizhou already in Zhou hands; two Generals of the Same Rites in the vanguard surrendered their commands to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 周兵擊顯州，執刺史陸瓊，復攻拔諸城。

translations.literal: Zhou troops attacked Xianzhou, seized Governor Lu Qiong, and again stormed and took the various cities.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou troops attacked Xianzhou, seized governor Lu Qiong, and stormed the other cities again.

sentences.zh: 紹義還保北朔州。

translations.literal: Shaoyi withdrew to hold North Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyi fell back to defend North Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 周東平公神舉將兵逼馬邑，紹義戰敗，北奔突厥，猶有眾三千人。

translations.literal: Zhou Duke of Dongping Shenju led troops to press Mayi; Shaoyi was defeated and fled north to the Turks, still with three thousand followers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Duke of Dongping Shenju pressed Mayi; Shaoyi was defeated and fled north to the Turks with three thousand men still at his side.

sentences.zh: 紹義令曰：「欲還者從其意。」

translations.literal: Shaoyi ordered: "Whoever wishes to return may do as he pleases."
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyi announced, "Whoever wishes to go back may do as he pleases."

sentences.zh: 於是辭去者大半。

translations.literal: Thereupon more than half took leave and departed.
translations.idiomatic: More than half then took their leave and departed.

sentences.zh: 突厥佗缽可汗常謂齊顯祖為英雄天子，以紹義重踝，似之，甚見愛重；

translations.literal: Tujue Khan Tuobo had often called Qi Emperor Xianzu a heroic Son of Heaven; seeing Shaoyi's heavy ankles, he thought him similar and greatly favored him;
translations.idiomatic: Tujue khan Tuobo had often called Qi Emperor Xianzu a heroic Son of Heaven; Shaoyi's heavy ankles reminded him of Xianzu, and the khan greatly favored him.

sentences.zh: 凡齊人在北者，悉以隸之。

translations.literal: all Qi people in the north were placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: All Qi subjects in the north were placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 於是齊之行台、州、鎮，唯東雍州行台傅伏、營州刺史高寶寧不下，其餘皆入於周。

translations.literal: Thereupon of Qi's mobile offices, prefectures, and garrisons, only Eastern Yongzhou Mobile Office Fu Fu and Governor of Yingzhou Gao Baoning did not submit; the rest all entered Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Of Qi's mobile offices, prefectures, and garrisons, only Eastern Yongzhou mobile office chief Fu Fu and Yingzhou governor Gao Baoning held out; the rest all submitted to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 凡得州五十，郡一百六十二，縣三百八十，戶三百三萬二千五百。

translations.literal: In all they gained fifty prefectures, one hundred sixty-two commanderies, three hundred eighty counties, and three million two hundred twenty-five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In all they gained fifty prefectures, one hundred sixty-two commanderies, three hundred eighty counties, and 3,022,500 households.

sentences.zh: 高寶寧者，齊之疏屬，有勇略，久鎮和龍，甚得夷、夏之心。

translations.literal: Gao Baoning was a distant kinsman of Qi, brave and resourceful; long stationed at Helong, he had won the hearts of both barbarians and Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Baoning was a distant kinsman of the Qi royal house, brave and resourceful; long stationed at Helong, he had won the hearts of both nomads and Chinese.

sentences.zh: 周主於河陽、幽、青、南兗、豫、徐、北朔、定置總管府，相、並二州各置宮及六府官。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler established overall-command offices at Heyang, You, Qing, Southern Yan, Yu, Xu, North Shuozhou, and Ding; at Xiang and Bing he set palaces and officials of the Six Offices.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor established overall-command offices at Heyang, You, Qing, Southern Yan, Yu, Xu, North Shuozhou, and Ding, and set palaces and Six Offices officials at Xiang and Bing.

sentences.zh: 周師之克晉陽也，齊使開府儀同三司紇奚永安求救於突厥，比至，齊已亡。

translations.literal: When the Zhou army took Jinyang, Qi sent General of the Open Office with Equal Honor in Three Departments Hexi Yong'an to seek aid from the Turks; by the time he arrived, Qi had perished.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou army took Jinyang, Qi sent General of the Open Office with Equal Honor in Three Departments Hexi Yong'an to seek aid from the Turks; by the time he arrived, Qi was gone.

sentences.zh: 佗缽可汗處永安於吐谷渾使者之下，永安言於佗缽曰：「今齊國已亡，永安何用餘生！

translations.literal: Khan Tuobo seated Yong'an below the Tuyuhun envoy; Yong'an said to Tuobo: "Now that Great Qi is destroyed, of what use is Yong'an's remaining life!
translations.idiomatic: Khan Tuobo seated Yong'an below the Tuyuhun envoy; Yong'an said to Tuobo, "Great Qi is destroyed—what use is my life now!

sentences.zh: 欲閉氣自絕，恐天下謂大齊無死節之臣；

translations.literal: I wish to hold my breath and end myself, but fear the world will say Great Qi had no minister who died for principle;
translations.idiomatic: I would hold my breath and die, but fear the world will say Great Qi had no minister who died for principle.

sentences.zh: 乞賜一刀，以顯示遠近。」

translations.literal: I beg you grant a blade to show near and far."
translations.idiomatic: Grant me a blade, that all near and far may see."

sentences.zh: 佗缽嘉之，贈馬七十匹而歸之。

translations.literal: Tuobo admired him, gave seventy horses as gifts, and sent him home.
translations.idiomatic: Tuobo admired him, gave him seventy horses, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 6梁主入朝於鄴。

translations.literal: 6. The Liang ruler came to court at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: 6. The Liang emperor came to court at Ye.

sentences.zh: 自秦兼天下，無朝覲之禮，至是始命有司草具其事：致積，致食氣，設九儐、九介，受享於廟，三公、三孤、六卿致食，勞賓，還贄，致享，皆如古禮。

translations.literal: Since Qin united the realm there had been no court-audience rites; now for the first time he ordered the officials to draft the procedures: presenting stores, presenting food and drink, setting nine hosts and nine envoys, receiving tribute in the temple, the Three Dukes, Three Solitaries, and Six Ministers presenting food, comforting the guest, returning gifts, presenting offerings—all according to ancient ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Since Qin united the realm there had been no court-audience rites; now for the first time he ordered officials to draft the procedures—presenting stores and food and drink, setting nine hosts and nine envoys, receiving tribute in the temple, the Three Dukes, Three Solitaries, and Six Ministers presenting food, comforting the guest, returning gifts, presenting offerings—all according to ancient ritual.

sentences.zh: 周主與梁主宴，酒酣，周主自彈琵琶。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler feasted with the Liang ruler; when the wine was warm, the Zhou ruler himself played the pipa.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor feasted with the Liang emperor; when the wine was warm, the Zhou emperor played the pipa himself.

sentences.zh: 梁主起舞，曰：「陛下既親撫五弦，臣何敢不同百獸！」

translations.literal: The Liang ruler rose to dance, saying: "Your Majesty has himself plucked the five strings—how dare your servant not join the hundred beasts!"
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor rose to dance and said, "Your Majesty has plucked the five strings himself—how dare I not join the hundred beasts!"

sentences.zh: 周主大悅，賜賚甚厚。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler was greatly pleased and gave lavish rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor was greatly pleased and gave lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，周主自鄴西還。

translations.literal: On yimao the Zhou ruler returned west from Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao the Zhou emperor returned west from Ye.

sentences.zh: 7三月，壬午，周詔：「山東諸軍，各舉明經干治者二人；

translations.literal: 7. In the third month, on renwu, Zhou decreed: "Each army east of the mountains shall recommend two men versed in the Classics and capable in administration;
translations.idiomatic: 7. In the third month, on renwu, Zhou decreed, "Each army east of the mountains shall recommend two men versed in the Classics and capable in administration.

sentences.zh: 若奇才異術，卓爾不群者，不拘此數。」

translations.literal: if there are men of extraordinary talent and rare skill, outstanding and unmatched, they are not bound by this number."
translations.idiomatic: Men of extraordinary talent and rare skill who stand far above the rest are not bound by this number."

sentences.zh: 周主之擒尉相貴也，招齊東雍州刺史傅伏，伏不從。

translations.literal: When the Zhou ruler captured Wei Xianggui, he summoned Qi Governor of Eastern Yongzhou Fu Fu, but Fu would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou emperor captured Wei Xianggui, he summoned Qi Eastern Yongzhou governor Fu Fu, but Fu refused.

sentences.zh: 齊人以伏為行台右僕射。

translations.literal: The Qi made Fu Right Vice Director of the Mobile Office.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi made Fu right vice director of the mobile office.

sentences.zh: 周主既克并州，復遣韋孝寬招之，令其子以上大將軍、武鄉公告身及金、馬腦二酒鐘賜伏為信。

translations.literal: After the Zhou ruler had taken Bingzhou, he again sent Wei Xiaokuan to summon him, having his son bring as tokens the rank of Senior General, the noble patent of Duke of Wuxiang, and two wine goblets of gold and agate.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhou emperor took Bingzhou, he sent Wei Xiaokuan again to summon him, with his son bearing the rank of senior general, the patent of Duke of Wuxiang, and two wine goblets of gold and agate as tokens.

sentences.zh: 伏不受，謂孝寬曰：「事君有死無貳。

translations.literal: Fu would not accept and said to Xiaokuan: "Serving one's lord admits death but not disloyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Fu refused and told Xiaokuan, "Serving one's lord admits death but not disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 此兒為臣不能竭忠，為子不能盡孝，人所讎疾，願速斬之以令天下！」

translations.literal: This boy as a minister cannot exhaust loyalty, as a son cannot fulfill filial duty—men loathe him; I beg you swiftly behead him to instruct the realm!"
translations.idiomatic: This boy cannot be loyal as a minister or filial as a son—men loathe him; behead him at once to instruct the realm!"

sentences.zh: 周主自鄴還，至晉州，遣高阿那肱等百餘人臨汾水召伏。

translations.literal: When the Zhou ruler returned from Ye and reached Jinzhou, he sent Gao Anagong and more than a hundred others to the Fen River to summon Fu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou emperor returned from Ye and reached Jinzhou, he sent Gao Anagong and more than a hundred men to the Fen River to summon Fu.

sentences.zh: 伏出軍，隔水見之，問：「至尊今何在？」

translations.literal: Fu led his army out, saw them across the water, and asked: "Where is His Majesty now?"
translations.idiomatic: Fu marched out, saw them across the water, and asked, "Where is His Majesty now?"

sentences.zh: 阿那肱曰：「已被擒矣。」

translations.literal: Anagong said: "He has already been captured."
translations.idiomatic: Anagong said, "He has already been captured."

sentences.zh: 伏仰天大哭，帥眾入城，於聽事前北面哀號，良久，然後降。

translations.literal: Fu looked to heaven and wept loudly, led his troops into the city, and before the audience hall wailed facing north for a long time before submitting.
translations.idiomatic: Fu looked to heaven and wept, led his troops into the city, and before the audience hall wailed facing north for a long time before he submitted.

sentences.zh: 周主見之曰：「何不早下？」

translations.literal: When the Zhou ruler saw him he said: "Why did you not submit earlier?"
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor said to him, "Why did you not submit earlier?"

sentences.zh: 伏流涕對曰：「臣三世為齊臣，食齊祿，不能自死，羞見天地！」

translations.literal: Fu answered through tears: "Your servant's family for three generations were Qi ministers, eating Qi's salary; unable to die for the state, I am ashamed to face heaven and earth!"
translations.idiomatic: Fu answered through tears, "Three generations of my family served Qi and ate Qi's salary; unable to die for the state, I am ashamed to face heaven and earth!"

sentences.zh: 周主執其手曰：「為臣當如此。」

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler took his hand and said: "A minister should be like this."
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor took his hand and said, "A minister should be like this."

sentences.zh: 乃以所食羊肋骨賜伏曰：「骨親肉疏，所以相付。」

translations.literal: He then gave Fu a sheep rib bone from his own meal, saying: "Bone is close, flesh is distant—therefore I entrust this to you."
translations.idiomatic: He gave Fu a sheep rib from his own meal and said, "Bone is close, flesh is distant—that is why I entrust this to you."

sentences.zh: 遂引使宿衛，授上儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: He then took him into palace guard service and appointed him Senior General of the Same Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He then took him into palace guard service and made him senior general of the same rites.

sentences.zh: 敕之曰：「若亟與公高官，恐歸附者心動。

translations.literal: He charged him: "If I swiftly give you high office, I fear those who submit will waver in heart.
translations.idiomatic: He told him, "If I give you high office at once, those who submit may waver in heart.

sentences.zh: 努力事朕，勿憂富貴。」

translations.literal: Serve me diligently; do not worry about wealth and rank."
translations.idiomatic: Serve me diligently; do not worry about wealth and rank."

sentences.zh: 他日，又問：「前救河陰得何賞？」

translations.literal: Another day he asked again: "When you previously rescued Heyin, what reward did you receive?"
translations.idiomatic: Another day he asked, "When you saved Heyin before, what reward did you receive?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「蒙一轉，授特進、永昌郡公。」

translations.literal: He answered: "I received one promotion—to Special Advancement and Duke of Yongchang Commandery."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "One promotion—to special advancement and Duke of Yongchang commandery."

sentences.zh: 周主謂高緯曰：「朕三年教戰，決取河陰。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler said to Gao Wei: "I trained for war three years and resolved to take Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor said to Gao Wei, "I trained for war three years and resolved to take Heyin.

sentences.zh: 正為傅伏善守，城不可動，遂斂軍而退。

translations.literal: It was precisely because Fu Fu defended well that the city could not be moved, and I therefore drew off the army and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: It was precisely because Fu Fu defended so well that the city would not budge, so I drew off the army and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 公當時賞功，何其薄也！」

translations.literal: How meager was your reward for merit at the time!"
translations.idiomatic: How meager your reward for merit was!"

sentences.zh: 8夏，四月，乙巳，周主至長安，置高緯於前，列其王公於後，車輿、旗幟、器物，以次陳之。

translations.literal: 8. In summer, the fourth month, on yisi, the Zhou ruler reached Chang'an, placed Gao Wei in front, ranged his princes and dukes behind, and displayed chariots, banners, and vessels in order.
translations.idiomatic: 8. In summer, the fourth month, on yisi, the Zhou emperor reached Chang'an, placed Gao Wei in front, ranged his princes and dukes behind, and displayed chariots, banners, and vessels in order.

sentences.zh: 備大駕，布六軍，奏凱樂，獻俘於太廟。

translations.literal: The great imperial equipage was prepared, the Six Armies arrayed, victory music played, and captives presented in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The great imperial equipage was prepared, the six armies arrayed, victory music played, and captives presented in the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 觀者皆稱萬歲。

translations.literal: The onlookers all shouted "Long live the emperor!".
translations.idiomatic: The onlookers all shouted "Long live the emperor!".

sentences.zh: 戊申，封高緯為溫公，齊之諸王三十餘人，皆受封爵。

translations.literal: On wushen Gao Wei was enfeoffed as Duke of Wen; more than thirty Qi princes all received titles and fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Gao Wei was enfeoffed as Duke of Wen, and more than thirty Qi princes all received titles and fiefs.

sentences.zh: 周主與齊君臣飲酒，令溫公起舞。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler drank with Qi ministers and lords and ordered the Duke of Wen to dance.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor drank with the Qi ministers and lords and ordered the Duke of Wen to dance.

sentences.zh: 高延宗悲不自持，屢欲仰藥，其傅婢禁止之。

translations.literal: Gao Yanzong was so grief-stricken he could not control himself; repeatedly he wished to take poison, but his tutor and maidservants restrained him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yanzong was overcome with grief; again and again he tried to take poison, but his tutor and maidservants stopped him.

sentences.zh: 周主以李德林為內史上士，自是詔誥格式用山東人物，並以委之。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler made Li Delin Senior Scribe of the Inner Court; thereafter edicts, proclamations, and formats employed men from east of the mountains, all entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor made Li Delin senior scribe of the inner court; thereafter edicts, proclamations, and formats employed men from east of the mountains, all entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 帝從容謂群臣曰：「我常日唯聞李德林名，復見其為齊朝作詔書移檄，正謂是天上人；

translations.literal: The emperor said calmly to his ministers: "In ordinary days I heard only Li Delin's name; then I saw his edicts and proclamations for the Qi court and thought he must be a man from heaven;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said calmly to his ministers, "In ordinary days I heard only Li Delin's name; when I saw the edicts and proclamations he wrote for Qi I thought he must be a man from heaven.

sentences.zh: 豈言今日得其驅使。」

translations.literal: who would have said that today I could have him at my command."
translations.idiomatic: Who would have said that today I could have him at my command."

sentences.zh: 神武公紇豆陵毅對曰：「臣聞麒麟鳳皇，為王者瑞，可以德感，不可力致。

translations.literal: Duke of Shenwu Yidouling Yi replied: "Your servant has heard that the qilin and phoenix are auspicious signs for a king—they may be moved by virtue, not seized by force.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Shenwu Yidouling Yi replied, "I have heard that the qilin and phoenix are auspicious signs for a king—they may be drawn by virtue, not seized by force.

sentences.zh: 麒麟鳳皇，得之無用。

translations.literal: The qilin and phoenix, if obtained, are of no use.
translations.idiomatic: The qilin and phoenix, if obtained, are of no use.

sentences.zh: 豈如德林，為瑞且有用哉！」

translations.literal: How can they compare with Delin, who is both an auspice and useful!"
translations.idiomatic: How can they compare with Delin, who is both an auspice and useful!"

sentences.zh: 帝大笑曰：「誠如公言。」

translations.literal: The emperor laughed greatly and said: "Truly as you say."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "Truly as you say."

sentences.zh: 9己巳，周主享太廟。

translations.literal: 9. On jisi the Zhou ruler offered in the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: 9. On jisi the Zhou emperor offered in the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁丑，周以譙王儉為大塚宰。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on dingchou, Zhou appointed Prince Qiao Jian as Grand Steward.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on dingchou, Zhou appointed Prince Qiao Jian grand steward.

sentences.zh: 庚辰。

translations.literal: On gengchen.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen.

sentences.zh: 以杞公亮為大司徒，鄭公達奚震為大宗伯，梁公侯莫陳芮為大司馬，應公獨孤永業為大司寇，鄭公韋孝寬為大司空。

translations.literal: Duke of Qi Liang was made Grand Minister of Education, Duke of Zheng Daxi Zhen Grand Minister of Rites, Duke of Liang Houmochen Rui Grand Minister of War, Duke of Ying Dugu Yongye Grand Minister of Justice, and Duke of Zheng Wei Xiaokuan Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Qi Liang was made grand minister of education, Duke of Zheng Daxi Zhen grand minister of rites, Duke of Liang Houmochen Rui grand minister of war, Duke of Ying Dugu Yongye grand minister of justice, and Duke of Zheng Wei Xiaokuan grand minister of works.

sentences.zh: 己丑，周主祭方丘。

translations.literal: On jichou the Zhou ruler sacrificed at the Square Mound.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou the Zhou emperor sacrificed at the Square Mound.

sentences.zh: 詔以「路寢會義、崇信、含仁、雲和、思齊諸殿，皆晉公護專政時所為，事窮壯麗，有逾清廟，悉可毀撤。

translations.literal: He decreed: "The halls of the Road Chamber—Huiyi, Chongxin, Hanren, Yunhe, Siqi, and the rest—were all built when Duke of Jin Hu monopolized power; their extravagance exceeded the Clear Temple and may all be torn down.
translations.idiomatic: He decreed, "The halls of the Road Chamber—Huiyi, Chongxin, Hanren, Yunhe, Siqi, and the rest—were all built when Duke of Jin Hu held power; their extravagance exceeded the Clear Temple and shall all be torn down.

sentences.zh: 雕斫之物，並賜貧民。

translations.literal: Carved objects shall all be given to the poor.
translations.idiomatic: Carved objects shall all be given to the poor.

sentences.zh: 繕造之宜，務從卑樸。」

translations.literal: In repairs and construction, strive for lowliness and simplicity."
translations.idiomatic: In repairs and construction, strive for simplicity and restraint."

sentences.zh: 戊戌，又詔：「並、鄴諸堂殿壯麗者准此。」

translations.literal: On wuxu he decreed again: "The grand halls of Bing and Ye shall follow this standard."
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu he decreed again, "The grand halls of Bing and Ye shall follow this standard."

sentences.zh: ::臣光曰：周高祖可謂善處勝矣！

translations.literal: Your servant Guang says: Zhou Gaozu may be called skilled in handling victory!
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang comments: Zhou Gaozu may be called skilled in handling victory!

sentences.zh: 他人勝則益奢，高祖勝而愈儉。

translations.literal: When others win they grow more extravagant; when Gaozu won he became more frugal.
translations.idiomatic: When others win they grow more extravagant; when Gaozu won he became more frugal.

sentences.zh: 10六月，丁卯，周主東巡。

translations.literal: 10. In the sixth month, on dingmao, the Zhou ruler toured east.
translations.idiomatic: 10. In the sixth month, on dingmao, the Zhou emperor toured east.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙戌，幸洛州。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingxu, he visited Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on bingxu, he visited Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬寅，議定權衡度量，頒之於四方。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on renyin, weights and measures were deliberated and fixed and promulgated to the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renyin, weights and measures were fixed and promulgated to the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 初，魏虜西涼之人，沒為隸戶，齊氏因之，仍供廝役。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wei had captured people of Western Liang and made them bond households; Qi continued the practice, still supplying menial service.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wei had captured people of Western Liang and made them bond households; Qi continued the practice, still supplying menial service.

sentences.zh: 周主滅齊，欲施寬惠，詔曰：「罪不及嗣，古有定科。

translations.literal: When the Zhou ruler destroyed Qi he wished to show leniency and decreed: "Punishment does not reach descendants—antiquity had fixed statutes for this.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou emperor destroyed Qi he wished to show leniency and decreed, "Punishment does not reach descendants—antiquity had fixed statutes for this.

sentences.zh: 雜役之徒，獨異常憲，一從罪配，百代不免，罰既無窮，刑何以措！

translations.literal: Yet men of miscellaneous service alone differ from ordinary law: once assigned for crime, for a hundred generations they are not released—when punishment is endless, how can punishments be set aside!
translations.idiomatic: Yet men of miscellaneous service alone stand outside ordinary law: once assigned for crime, for a hundred generations they are not released—when punishment is endless, how can punishments be set aside!

sentences.zh: 凡諸雜戶，悉放為民。」

translations.literal: All miscellaneous households shall be released as commoners."
translations.idiomatic: All miscellaneous households shall be released as commoners."

sentences.zh: 自是無複雜戶。

translations.literal: From this there were no more miscellaneous households.
translations.idiomatic: From this there were no more miscellaneous households.

sentences.zh: 甲子，鄭州獲九尾狐，已死，獻其骨。

translations.literal: On jiazi Zhengzhou captured a nine-tailed fox, already dead, and presented its bones.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Zhengzhou captured a nine-tailed fox, already dead, and presented its bones.

sentences.zh: 周主曰：「瑞應之來，必彰有德。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler said: "When auspicious responses come, they must display one who possesses virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor said, "When auspicious signs appear, they must display one who possesses virtue.

sentences.zh: 若五品時敘，四海和平，乃能致此。

translations.literal: Only if the five ranks are timely ordered and the four seas are at peace can such things be brought forth.
translations.idiomatic: Only if the five ranks are timely ordered and the four seas are at peace can such things be brought forth.

sentences.zh: 今無其時，恐非實錄。」

translations.literal: Now there is no such season; I fear this is not a true record."
translations.idiomatic: The time is not right; I fear this omen is not genuine.

sentences.zh: 命焚之。

translations.literal: He ordered it burned.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered it burned.

sentences.zh: 11九月，戊寅，周制：「庶人已上，唯聽衣綢、綿綢、絲布、圓綾、紗、絹、綃、葛、布等九種，余悉禁之。

translations.literal: 11. In the ninth month, on wuyin, Zhou regulation: "For commoners and above, only these nine kinds of dress are permitted: silk gauze, cotton silk, silk cloth, round twill, gauze, thin silk, crepe silk, ramie, and plain cloth; all else is forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: 11. In the ninth month, on wuyin, Zhou decreed: "Commoners and above may wear only nine kinds of cloth—silk gauze, cotton silk, silk cloth, round twill, gauze, thin silk, crepe silk, ramie, and plain cloth; everything else is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 朝祭之服，不拘此制。」

translations.literal: Court and sacrifice garments are not bound by this rule."
translations.idiomatic: Court and sacrificial dress is exempt from this rule."

sentences.zh: 12冬，十月，戊申，周主如鄴。

translations.literal: 12. In winter, the tenth month, on wushen, the Zhou ruler went to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: 12. In winter, the tenth month, on wushen, the Zhou emperor went to Ye.

sentences.zh: 13上聞周人滅齊，欲爭徐、兗，詔南兗州刺史、司空吳明徹督諸軍伐之，以其世子戎昭、將軍惠覺攝行州事。

translations.literal: 13. The Sovereign heard that the Zhou had destroyed Qi and wished to contest Xu and Yan; he decreed that Wu Mingche, Minister of Works and inspector of Southern Yanzhou, should command the armies in an expedition against them, and that his heir Zhaorong and the general Hui Jue should act in his place at the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: 13. The Chen emperor heard that the Zhou had destroyed Qi and wished to seize Xu and Yan; he ordered Wu Mingche, Minister of Works and inspector of Southern Yanzhou, to command the armies against them, while his heir Zhaorong and the general Hui Jue would govern the prefecture in his stead.

sentences.zh: 明徹軍至呂梁，周徐州總管梁士彥帥眾拒戰，戊午，明徹擊破之。

translations.literal: Wu Mingche's army reached Lüliang; Liang Shiyan, Zhou commissioner of Xuzhou, led troops to resist; on wuwu Mingche routed them.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Mingche's army reached Lüliang. Liang Shiyan, the Zhou commissioner of Xuzhou, led troops to resist; on wuwu Mingche defeated him.

sentences.zh: 士彥嬰城自守，明徹圍之。

translations.literal: Shiyan clung to the city in defense; Mingche besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan held the city and defended it; Mingche laid siege.

sentences.zh: 帝銳意以為河南指麾可定。

translations.literal: The emperor was keen to believe that south of the Yellow River could be settled at a wave of the hand.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen emperor was convinced that the lands south of the Yellow River could be taken at a gesture.

sentences.zh: 中書通事舍人蔡景歷諫曰：「師老將驕，不宜過窮遠略。」

translations.literal: Cai Jingli, Master of Documents and communications attendant, remonstrated, saying: "The army is weary and the generals proud; one should not press a distant strategy too far."
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jingli, Master of Documents and communications attendant, remonstrated: "The troops are exhausted and the generals overconfident; you should not drive this distant campaign to extremes."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，以為沮眾，出為豫章內史。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, taking this as damping morale, and sent him out as interior minister of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, took this as discouraging the host, and sent him out to be interior minister of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 未行，有飛章劾景歷在省贓污狼籍，坐免官，削爵土。

translations.literal: Before he had departed, a flying memorial accused Jingli of corruption and filth in the ministry; he was removed from office and stripped of fief and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave, an urgent memorial accused Jingli of rampant corruption in the ministry; he was dismissed, stripped of title and fief.

sentences.zh: 14周改葬德皇帝於冀州，周主服縗，哭於太極殿；

translations.literal: 14. Zhou reburied the Virtuous Emperor in Jizhou; the Zhou ruler wore hemp mourning and wept in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate;
translations.idiomatic: 14. Zhou reburied the Virtuous Emperor in Jizhou; the Zhou emperor wore mourning hemp and wept in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate;

sentences.zh: 百官素服。

translations.literal: the hundred officials wore white mourning.
translations.idiomatic: the hundred officials wore white mourning.

sentences.zh: 15周人誣溫公高緯與宜州刺史穆提婆謀反，並其宗族皆賜死。

translations.literal: 15. The Zhou people falsely charged Duke of Wen Gao Wei and Yizhou inspector Mu Tipo with plotting rebellion, and granted death to them and all their clans.
translations.idiomatic: 15. The Zhou falsely accused Duke of Wen Gao Wei and Yizhou inspector Mu Tipo of rebellion and put them and their entire clans to death.

sentences.zh: 眾人多自陳無之，高延宗獨攘袂泣而不言，以椒塞口而死。

translations.literal: Many of the multitude pleaded their innocence; Gao Yanzong alone flung his sleeve and wept without speaking, and died with pepper stuffed in his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Most pleaded innocence; Gao Yanzong alone flung back his sleeve, wept in silence, and died with pepper stuffed in his mouth.

sentences.zh: 唯緯弟仁英以清狂，仁雅以瘖疾得免，徙於蜀。

translations.literal: Only Wei's younger brothers Renying, for pure madness, and Renya, for dumb illness, were spared and moved to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wei's younger brothers Renying, deemed feeble-minded, and Renya, mute from illness, were spared and exiled to Shu.

sentences.zh: 其餘親屬，不殺者散配西土，皆死於邊裔。

translations.literal: The rest of the kin, those not killed, were scattered to the western lands and all died on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The rest of the kin, those not executed, were scattered across the western marches and perished on the borders.

sentences.zh: 周主以高湝妻盧氏賜其將斛斯征。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler gave Gao Shao's wife Lady Lu to his general Husi Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor gave Gao Shao's wife, Lady Lu, to his general Husi Zheng.

sentences.zh: 盧氏蓬首垢面，長齋，不言笑。

translations.literal: Lady Lu wore tangled hair and a filthy face, kept long fasts, and neither spoke nor smiled.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Lu let her hair tangle and her face go filthy, kept perpetual fasts, and neither spoke nor smiled.

sentences.zh: 征放之，乃為尼。

translations.literal: Zheng released her, and she became a nun.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng released her, and she took the veil.

sentences.zh: 齊後、妃貧者，至以賣燭為業。

translations.literal: Poor Qi empresses and consorts came even to selling candles for a living.
translations.idiomatic: Qi empresses and consorts reduced to poverty sold candles for a living.

sentences.zh: 16十一月，壬申，周立皇子衍為道王，兌為蔡王。

translations.literal: 16. In the eleventh month, on renshen, Zhou enfeoffed the princes Yan as Prince of Dao and Dui as Prince of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: 16. In the eleventh month, on renshen, Zhou enfeoffed Prince Yan as Prince of Dao and Prince Dui as Prince of Cai.

sentences.zh: 17癸酉，周遣上大將軍王軌將兵救徐州。

translations.literal: 17. On guiyou Zhou sent Grand General Wang Gui to lead troops to rescue Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: 17. On guiyou Zhou dispatched Grand General Wang Gui to lead troops to relieve Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，周人敗齊師於晉州，乘勝逐北。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Zhou had defeated Qi forces at Jinzhou and pursued north in victory.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Zhou had routed the Qi at Jinzhou and pressed the pursuit northward.

sentences.zh: 齊人所棄甲仗，未暇收斂，稽胡乘間竊出，並盜而有之。

translations.literal: The armor and weapons the Qi had abandoned, with no time to gather in, the Jiehu stole out in the interval and seized them all.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had abandoned armor and weapons with no time to recover them; the Jiehu slipped out in the gap and made off with the lot.

sentences.zh: 仍立劉蠡升之孫沒鐸為主，號聖武皇帝，改元石平。

translations.literal: They then set up Mo Duo, grandson of Liu Lisheng, as lord, styled Holy Martial Emperor, and changed the era name to Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: They enthroned Liu Lisheng's grandson Mo Duo as Holy Martial Emperor and adopted the era name Shiping.

sentences.zh: 周人既克關東，將討稽胡，議欲窮其巢穴。

translations.literal: The Zhou, having taken the eastern lands, were about to campaign against the Jiehu and debated exhausting their nests.
translations.idiomatic: After conquering the eastern lands, the Zhou prepared to subdue the Jiehu and debated rooting out their nests entirely.

sentences.zh: 齊王憲曰：「步落稽種類既多，又山谷險絕，王師一舉，未可盡除。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Xian said: "The Buzhuo Jie are many in kind, and their valleys are perilous and cut off; one stroke of the royal army cannot root them all out.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Xian said: "The Buzhuo Jie are many tribes in rugged mountain country; a single royal campaign cannot exterminate them all.

sentences.zh: 且當剪其魁首，余加慰撫。」

translations.literal: For now cut off their chiefs; the rest add comfort and soothing."
translations.idiomatic: Cut down the leaders for now and soothe the rest."

sentences.zh: 周主從之，以憲為行軍元帥，督諸軍討之。

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler followed this, making Xian marshal of the campaign and commanding the armies against them.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor agreed, appointing Xian campaign marshal to direct the punitive armies.

sentences.zh: 至馬邑，分道俱進。

translations.literal: Reaching Mayi, they divided forces and advanced together.
translations.idiomatic: At Mayi they split into columns and advanced together.

sentences.zh: 沒鐸分遣其黨天柱守河東，穆支守河西，據險以拒之。

translations.literal: Mo Duo sent his partisans Tianzhu to hold Hedong and Muzhi to hold Hexi, holding the passes to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Duo sent his followers Tianzhu to hold Hedong and Muzhi to hold Hexi, blocking the passes.

sentences.zh: 憲命譙王儉擊天柱，滕王逌擊穆支，並破之，斬首萬餘級。

translations.literal: Xian ordered Prince of Qiao Jian to strike Tianzhu and Prince of Teng You to strike Muzhi; both were broken, and more than ten thousand heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Xian sent Prince of Qiao Jian against Tianzhu and Prince of Teng You against Muzhi; both were crushed, with more than ten thousand heads taken.

sentences.zh: 趙王招擊沒鐸，擒之，餘眾皆降。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Zhao attacked Mo Duo and captured him; the rest all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhao Zhao attacked Mo Duo, captured him, and the remainder surrendered.

sentences.zh: 18周詔：「自永熙三年以來，東土之民掠為奴婢，及克江陵之日，良人沒為奴婢者，並放為良。」

translations.literal: 18. Zhou decree: "Since Yongxi year 3, eastern land people seized as slave-servants, and on the day Jiangling fell, good people made slave-servants—all are released as good people."
translations.idiomatic: 18. Zhou decreed: "Since the third year of Yongxi, easterners seized as slaves, and those made slaves when Jiangling fell—all are restored to free status."

sentences.zh: 又詔：「後宮唯置妃二人，世婦三人，御妻三人，此外皆減之。」

translations.literal: Also a decree: "In the rear palace only two consorts, three palace ladies, and three imperial wives are to be kept; all beyond this are reduced."
translations.idiomatic: Another decree: "The rear palace shall keep only two consorts, three palace ladies, and three imperial wives; all others are dismissed."

sentences.zh: 周主性節儉，常服布袍，寢布被，後宮不過十餘人；

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler was by nature frugal; he regularly wore cloth robes and slept under cloth quilts; the rear palace did not exceed a dozen persons;
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor was frugal by nature, wore plain cloth robes, slept under cloth quilts, and kept fewer than a dozen women in the rear palace;

sentences.zh: 每行兵，親在行陳，步涉山谷，人所不堪；

translations.literal: on every campaign he was personally in the battle line, wading valleys on foot where men could not endure it;
translations.idiomatic: on campaign he marched in the ranks himself, footing valleys on foot that broke ordinary men;

sentences.zh: 撫將士有恩，而明察果斷，用法嚴峻。

translations.literal: he treated officers with grace yet was clear-sighted and resolute, applying the law with severity.
translations.idiomatic: he showed officers kindness yet was sharp-eyed and decisive, enforcing the law without mercy.

sentences.zh: 由是將士畏威而樂為之死。

translations.literal: Thus soldiers feared his authority yet were glad to die for him.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers feared his stern rule yet were glad to die for him.

sentences.zh: 19己亥晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: 19. On the last day of jihai, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: 19. On the last day of jihai, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 20周初行《刑書要制》：群盜贓一匹，及正、長隱五丁、若地頃以上，皆死。

translations.literal: 20. Zhou first implemented the Essential Regulations of the Penal Statutes: for bandit theft of one bolt of goods, and for rectifiers and chiefs hiding five households or land of one qing and above—all death.
translations.idiomatic: 20. Zhou first enforced the Essential Regulations of the Penal Statutes: theft of a single bolt, or village heads concealing five households or a qing of land—all punishable by death.

sentences.zh: 21十二月，戊申，新作東宮成，太子徙居之。

translations.literal: 21. In the twelfth month, on wushen, the new Eastern Palace was completed and the Crown Prince moved in.
translations.idiomatic: 21. In the twelfth month, on wushen, the new Eastern Palace was finished and the Crown Prince took residence.

sentences.zh: 22庚申，周主如并州，移并州軍民四萬戶於關中。

translations.literal: 22. On gengshen the Zhou ruler went to Bingzhou and moved forty thousand Bingzhou army households into Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: 22. On gengshen the Zhou emperor went to Bingzhou and relocated forty thousand Bingzhou households to Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，廢并州宮及六府。

translations.literal: On wuchen the Bingzhou palace and six ministries were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen the Bingzhou palace and six ministries were abolished.

sentences.zh: 23高寶寧自黃龍上表勸進於高紹義，紹義遂稱皇帝，改元武平，以寶寧為丞相。

translations.literal: 23. Gao Baoning from Huanglong submitted a memorial urging Gao Shaoyi to advance; Shaoyi then styled himself emperor, changed the era to Wuping, and made Baoning chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: 23. Gao Baoning of Huanglong memorialized urging Gao Shaoyi to take the throne; Shaoyi declared himself emperor, adopted the era Wuping, and made Baoning chancellor.

sentences.zh: 突厥佗缽可汗舉兵助之。

translations.literal: The Tujue Khan Tuobo raised troops to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: The Tujue khan Tuobo raised an army to support him.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，壬午，周主幸鄴；

translations.literal: 1. In spring, the first month, on renwu, the Zhou ruler visited Ye;
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, the first month, on renwu, the Zhou emperor visited Ye;

sentences.zh: 辛卯，幸懷州；

translations.literal: on xinmao he visited Huaizhou;
translations.idiomatic: on xinmao he visited Huaizhou;

sentences.zh: 癸巳，幸洛州。

translations.literal: on guisi he visited Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: on guisi he visited Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 置懷州宮。

translations.literal: The Huaizhou palace was established.
translations.idiomatic: A palace was established at Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 2二月，甲辰，周譙孝王儉卒。

translations.literal: 2. In the second month, on jiachen, Zhou Prince of Qiao Xiaowang Jian died.
translations.idiomatic: 2. In the second month, on jiachen, Zhou Prince of Qiao, Xiaowang Jian, died.

sentences.zh: 3丁巳，周主還長安。

translations.literal: 3. On dingsi the Zhou ruler returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: 3. On dingsi the Zhou emperor returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 4吳明徹圍周彭城，環列舟艦於城下，攻之甚急。

translations.literal: 4. Wu Mingche besieged Zhou Pengcheng, ranged warships in a ring below the walls, and pressed the assault fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: 4. Wu Mingche besieged Pengcheng, ringed the walls with warships, and pressed the attack relentlessly.

sentences.zh: 王軌引兵輕行，據淮口，結長圍，以鐵鎖貫車輪數百，沈之清水，以遏陳船歸路，軍中恟懼。

translations.literal: Wang Gui led troops by a light march, seized the Huai mouth, formed a long encirclement, ran iron chains through hundreds of chariot wheels, and sank them in the clear water to block the Chen ships' path home; the army was terror-stricken.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui marched lightly, seized the Huai mouth, drew a long encirclement, threaded iron chains through hundreds of chariot wheels, and sank them in the shallows to cut off the Chen fleet's retreat; panic spread through the army.

sentences.zh: 譙州刺史蕭摩訶言於明徹曰：「聞王軌始鎖下流，其兩端築城，今尚未立，公若見遣擊之，彼必不敢相拒。

translations.literal: Qiaozhou inspector Xiao Mohe said to Mingche: "I hear Wang Gui has begun to lock the lower stream; he is building walled ends at both sides, which are not yet complete—if you send me to strike them, they will surely not dare resist.
translations.idiomatic: Qiaozhou inspector Xiao Mohe told Mingche: "Wang Gui has begun to block the lower river and is building forts at both ends—they are not finished yet. Send me to attack, and they will not dare stand.

sentences.zh: 水路未斷，賊勢不堅；

translations.literal: The water route is not yet cut; the enemy's strength is not firm;
translations.idiomatic: The waterway is still open; their position is not yet secure;

sentences.zh: 彼城若立，則吾屬必為虜矣。

translations.literal: if those walls stand, then we shall surely become captives.
translations.idiomatic: once those forts stand, we are finished.

sentences.zh: 明徹奮髯曰：「搴旗陷陳，將軍事也；

translations.literal: Mingche bristled his beard and said: "Seizing banners and plunging into the array is a general's business;
translations.idiomatic: Mingche stroked his beard and said: "Seizing banners and breaking the line—that is a general's work;

sentences.zh: 長算遠略，老夫事也。」

translations.literal: long calculation and far strategy are this old man's business."
translations.idiomatic: grand strategy is this old man's work."

sentences.zh: 摩訶失色而退。

translations.literal: Mohe blanched and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Mohe turned pale and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 一旬之間，水路遂斷。

translations.literal: Within ten days the water route was cut.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days the waterway was sealed.

sentences.zh: 周兵益至，諸將議破堰拔軍，以舫載馬而去。

translations.literal: Zhou troops increased; the generals debated breaking the weir and withdrawing the army, carrying the horses away on boats.
translations.idiomatic: More Zhou troops arrived; the generals debated breaching the dam and withdrawing by boat with the horses.

sentences.zh: 馬主裴子烈曰：「若破堰下船，船必傾倒，不如先遣馬出。」

translations.literal: Master of horses Pei Zilie said: "If we break the weir and go downstream by boat, the boats will surely capsize—it is better to send the horses out first."
translations.idiomatic: Master of horses Pei Zilie said: "If we breach the dam and board, the boats will capsize—send the horses out first."

sentences.zh: 時明徹苦背疾甚篤，蕭摩訶復請曰：「今求戰不得，進退無路。

translations.literal: At this time Mingche suffered grievous back illness; Xiao Mohe petitioned again, saying: "Now we cannot obtain battle; advance and retreat have no road.
translations.idiomatic: Mingche was gravely ill with back pain; Xiao Mohe pleaded again: "We cannot force battle; there is no way forward or back.

sentences.zh: 若潛軍突圍，未足為恥。

translations.literal: If we slip the army through in a breakout, it is scarcely shameful.
translations.idiomatic: A stealthy breakout is no great shame.

sentences.zh: 願公帥步卒、乘馬輿徐行，摩訶領鐵騎數千驅馳前後，必當使公安達京邑。」

translations.literal: I wish you would lead foot soldiers and ride in a litter at an easy pace; Mohe will lead several thousand iron cavalry driving before and behind—this will surely bring you safe to the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Let you lead the foot soldiers in a litter at an easy pace; I will take several thousand iron cavalry before and behind—you will reach the capital safely."

sentences.zh: 明徹曰：「弟之此策，乃良圖也。

translations.literal: Mingche said: "Brother, this plan of yours is indeed a fine scheme.
translations.idiomatic: Mingche said: "Brother, that is sound counsel.

sentences.zh: 然步軍既多，吾為總督，必須身居其後，相帥兼行。

translations.literal: Yet the foot soldiers are many; as overall commander I must keep myself in the rear, leading together in combined march.
translations.idiomatic: But the foot are numerous; as commander I must bring up the rear and march with them.

sentences.zh: 弟馬軍宜須在前，不可遲緩。」

translations.literal: Brother's horse army must be in front; there must be no delay."
translations.idiomatic: Your cavalry must ride ahead—do not linger."

sentences.zh: 摩訶因帥馬軍夜發。

translations.literal: Mohe thereupon led the horse army away by night.
translations.idiomatic: Mohe led the cavalry away that night.

sentences.zh: 甲子，明徹決堰，乘水勢退軍。

translations.literal: On jiazi Mingche broke the weir and withdrew the army riding the water's force.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Mingche breached the dam and withdrew on the current.

sentences.zh: 冀以入淮。

translations.literal: He hoped to enter the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to reach the Huai.

sentences.zh: 至清口，水勢漸微，舟艦並礙車輪，不復得過。

translations.literal: Reaching Qingkou, the water's force gradually slackened; the warships all fouled the chariot wheels and could pass no more.
translations.idiomatic: At Qingkou the current weakened; the ships snagged on the sunken wheels and could not pass.

sentences.zh: 王軌引兵圍而蹙之，眾潰。

translations.literal: Wang Gui led troops to surround and press them; the host collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui closed in and crushed them; the army broke.

sentences.zh: 明徹為周人所執，將士三萬並器械輜重皆沒於周。

translations.literal: Mingche was seized by the Zhou; thirty thousand soldiers with weapons and baggage all fell to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mingche was captured; thirty thousand men, with arms and baggage, were lost to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 蕭摩訶以精騎八十居前突圍，眾騎繼之，比旦，達淮南，與將軍任忠、周羅□獨全軍得還。

translations.literal: Xiao Mohe with eighty elite cavalry led the van in breaking out; the mass of riders followed; by dawn they reached south of the Huai, and with the generals Ren Zhong and Zhou Luo□ alone brought the whole army back.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Mohe led eighty elite horsemen in the van to break out; the rest followed; by dawn they reached south of the Huai, and with the generals Ren Zhong and Zhou Luohou alone brought the army home intact.

sentences.zh: 初，帝謀取彭、汴，以問五兵尚書毛喜，對曰：「淮左新平，邊民未輯。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor planned to take Peng and Bian, he asked Mao Xi, Minister of the Five Arms, who replied: "The Huai left has newly been pacified; the frontier people are not yet settled.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Chen emperor planned to take Peng and Bian, he asked Mao Xi, Minister of the Five Arms, who said: "The Huai region has only just been pacified; the border people are not yet settled.

sentences.zh: 周氏始吞齊國，難與爭鋒。

translations.literal: Zhou has just swallowed Qi; it is hard to contend with their edge.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou has just swallowed Qi; this is no moment to test their strength.

sentences.zh: 且棄舟□戢之工，踐車騎之地，去長就短，非吳人所便。

translations.literal: Moreover to abandon boat□戢 craft and tread chariot and cavalry ground, leaving the long for the short, is not what Wu men find easy.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon boat□ warfare and oar craft for chariot and cavalry country—trading our strength for weakness—is not what men of Wu do well.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為不若安民保境，寢兵結好，斯久長之術也。」

translations.literal: I in my folly think it better to settle the people and guard the borders, lay down arms and join in friendship—this is the long-lasting art."
translations.idiomatic: I would settle the people, hold the borders, lay down arms, and seek peace—that is the lasting course."

sentences.zh: 及明徹敗，帝謂喜曰：「卿言驗於今矣。」

translations.literal: When Mingche was defeated, the emperor said to Xi: "Your words are verified today."
translations.idiomatic: After Mingche's defeat the emperor told Xi: "Your warning has proved true today."

sentences.zh: 即日，召蔡景歷，復以為征南咨議參軍。

translations.literal: That same day he recalled Cai Jingli and again made him staff adviser for the southern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he recalled Cai Jingli and restored him as staff adviser for the southern expedition.

sentences.zh: 5周主封吳明徹為懷德公，位大將軍。

translations.literal: 5. The Zhou ruler enfeoffed Wu Mingche as Duke of Huaide, with the rank of Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: 5. The Zhou emperor enfeoffed Wu Mingche as Duke of Huaide with the rank of Grand General.

sentences.zh: 明徹憂憤而卒。

translations.literal: Mingche died in grief and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Mingche died of grief and rage.

sentences.zh: 6乙丑，周以越王盛為大塚宰。
