translations.literal: 6. On yichou Zhou made Prince of Yue Sheng Grand Chamberlain.
translations.idiomatic: 6. On yichou Zhou appointed Prince of Yue Sheng Grand Chamberlain.

sentences.zh: 7三月，戊辰，周於蒲州置宮，廢同州及長春二宮。

translations.literal: 7. In the third month, on wuchen, Zhou established a palace at Puzhou and abolished the Tongzhou and Changchun palaces.
translations.idiomatic: 7. In the third month, on wuchen, Zhou built a palace at Puzhou and abolished the palaces at Tongzhou and Changchun.

sentences.zh: 8甲戌，周主初服常冠，以皁紗全幅向後襆發，仍裁為四腳。

translations.literal: 8. On jiaxu the Zhou ruler first wore the ordinary cap, folding the full width of black gauze back to bind the hair, then cutting it into four corners.
translations.idiomatic: 8. On jiaxu the Zhou emperor first wore the ordinary cap, wrapping a full width of black gauze back over the hair and cutting it into four corners.

sentences.zh: 9丙子，命中軍大將軍、開府儀同三司淳於量為大都督，總水陸諸軍事，鎮西將軍孫瑒督荊、郢諸軍，平北將軍樊毅都督清口上至荊山緣淮諸軍，寧遠將軍任忠都督壽陽、新蔡、霍州諸軍，以備周。

translations.literal: 9. On bingzi he appointed Grand General, Commissioner with the authority of an Opening of the Government Chunyu Liang as Grand Commander overseeing land and water forces, Western Garrison General Sun Chang to command Jing and Ying armies, Pacifier of the North Fan Yi to command from Qingkou up to Jingshan along the Huai, and Far-pacifying General Ren Zhong to command Shouyang, Xincai, and Huozhou armies, to guard against Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: 9. On bingzi he appointed Grand General Chunyu Liang, Commissioner with Opening of the Government authority, as Grand Commander of land and sea forces; Western Garrison General Sun Chang to command the Jing and Ying armies; Pacifier of the North Fan Yi to command the Huai from Qingkou to Jingshan; and Far-pacifying General Ren Zhong to command Shouyang, Xincai, and Huozhou—all to guard against Zhou.

sentences.zh: 10乙酉，大赦。

translations.literal: 10. On yiyou, a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: 10. On yiyou, a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 11壬辰，周改元宣政。

translations.literal: 11. On renchen Zhou changed the era name to Xuanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: 11. On renchen Zhou changed the era name to Xuanzheng.

sentences.zh: 12夏，四月，庚申，突厥寇周幽州，殺掠吏民。

translations.literal: 12. In summer, the fourth month, on gengshen, the Tujue raided Youzhou of Zhou and killed and plundered officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: 12. In summer, the fourth month, on gengshen, the Tujue raided Zhou's Youzhou, killing and plundering officials and people.

sentences.zh: 13戊午，樊毅遣軍渡淮北，對清口築城。

translations.literal: 13. On wuwu Fan Yi sent troops across the Huai north and built a city facing Qingkou.
translations.idiomatic: 13. On wuwu Fan Yi sent troops north of the Huai and built a city opposite Qingkou.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，清口城不守。

translations.literal: On renxu the Qingkou city could not be held.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Qingkou fell.

sentences.zh: 14五月，己丑，周高祖帥諸軍伐突厥，遣柱國原公姬願、東平公神舉等將兵五道俱入。

translations.literal: 14. In the fifth month, on jichou, Zhou Gaozu led the armies against the Tujue, dispatching the pillar Duke of Yuan Ji Yuan and Duke of Dongping Shenju and others to lead troops in five columns together inward.
translations.idiomatic: 14. In the fifth month, on jichou, Zhou Gaozu led the armies against the Tujue, sending the pillar Duke of Yuan Ji Yuan, Duke of Dongping Shenju, and others in five columns.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，帝不豫，留止雲陽宮；

translations.literal: On guisi the emperor was unwell and halted at the Yunyang Palace;
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the Zhou emperor fell ill and remained at the Yunyang Palace;

sentences.zh: 丙申，詔停諸軍。

translations.literal: on bingshen he decreed to halt all armies.
translations.idiomatic: on bingshen he ordered all armies to stand down.

sentences.zh: 驛召宗師宇文孝伯赴行在所，帝執其手曰：「吾自量必無濟理，以後事付君。」

translations.literal: By post-horse he summoned Imperial Preceptor Yuwen Xiaobo to the mobile headquarters; the emperor took his hand and said: "I myself judge that I surely cannot be saved; I entrust later affairs to you."
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Imperial Preceptor Yuwen Xiaobo by urgent relay to the imperial camp; the Zhou emperor took his hand and said, "I know in my heart that I cannot recover; I leave what comes after to you."

sentences.zh: 是夜，授孝伯司衛上大夫，總宿衛兵。

translations.literal: That night he appointed Xiaobo Senior Superintendent of the Palace Guard, in overall charge of the night guards.
translations.idiomatic: That night he made Xiaobo Senior Superintendent of the Palace Guards and put him in charge of all the night watch.

sentences.zh: 又令馳驛入京鎮守，以備非常。

translations.literal: He also ordered him to ride post-horses into the capital to garrison it against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered him to ride post-horses to the capital to hold it against any emergency.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁酉朔，帝疾甚，還長安；

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the first day of the month (dingyou), the emperor was gravely ill and returned to Chang'an;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the first day of the month (dingyou), the Zhou emperor grew critically ill and returned to Chang'an;

sentences.zh: 是夕殂，年三十六。

translations.literal: that evening he died, aged thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: that evening he died, at the age of thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 15戊戌，太子即位。

translations.literal: 15. On wuxu the crown prince ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: 15. On wuxu the crown prince took the throne.

sentences.zh: 尊皇后阿史那氏為皇太后。

translations.literal: The empress Ashina was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Ashina was elevated to empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 宣帝始立，即逞奢欲。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuān first took the throne, he at once indulged extravagant desires.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as Emperor Xuān came to the throne, he gave free rein to extravagance and lust.

sentences.zh: 大行在殯，曾無戚容，捫其杖痕，大罵曰：「死晚矣！」

translations.literal: While the late emperor lay in coffin, he showed not the least grief; he felt the marks of the staff and cursed loudly: "You died too late!"
translations.idiomatic: With his father still in the coffin, he showed no sign of mourning; he fingered the cane marks on his body and cursed aloud, "You should have died sooner!"

sentences.zh: 閱視高祖宮人，逼為淫慾。

translations.literal: He inspected Gaozu's palace women and forced them to his lust.
translations.idiomatic: He went through the palace women of Emperor Gaozu and forced them to satisfy his desires.

sentences.zh: 超拜吏部下大夫鄭譯為開府儀同大將軍、內史中大夫，委以朝政。

translations.literal: He promoted in one leap Zheng Yi of the Ministry of Personnel, a Grand Master of the Palace, to Grand General of the Palace with the same honors as the Three Excellencies and to Grand Master of the Palace Secretariat, and entrusted him with court government.
translations.idiomatic: He leapfrogged Zheng Yi, a junior minister in the Ministry of Personnel, to Grand General of the Palace with the honors of the Three Excellencies and Grand Master of the Palace Secretariat, and put the government in his hands.

sentences.zh: 己未，葬武皇帝於孝陵，廟號高祖。

translations.literal: On jiwei Emperor Wu was buried at Xiaoling; his temple name was Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Emperor Wu was buried at Xiaoling with the temple name Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 既葬，詔內外公除，帝及六宮皆議即吉。

translations.literal: After the burial, he decreed mourning ended inside and outside; the emperor and the six palaces all discussed observing immediate auspicious rites.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial he ordered mourning ended throughout the court and the realm; the emperor and the six palaces all debated ending mourning at once.

sentences.zh: 京兆郡丞樂運上疏，以為「葬期既促，事訖即除，太為汲汲。」

translations.literal: Yue Yun, assistant magistrate of Jingzhao commandery, submitted a memorial, holding that "the burial period was already rushed; when the affair was done to end mourning at once was far too hurried."
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yun, assistant magistrate of Jingzhao, memorialized that "the burial had already been rushed, and to end mourning as soon as it was over was far too hasty."

sentences.zh: 帝不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 帝以齊煬王憲屬尊望重，忌之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Prince Yang of Qi Xian was of honored standing and heavy prestige, envied him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor resented Prince Xian of Qi, the Prince Yang, for his rank and renown.

sentences.zh: 謂宇文孝伯曰：「公能為朕圖齊王，當以其官相授。」

translations.literal: He said to Yuwen Xiaobo: "If you can plot against the Prince of Qi for me, I shall grant you his office."
translations.idiomatic: He told Yuwen Xiaobo, "If you can rid me of the Prince of Qi, I will give you his post."

sentences.zh: 孝伯叩頭曰：「先帝遺詔，不許濫誅骨肉。

translations.literal: Xiaobo kowtowed and said: "The late emperor's testament forbade wanton execution of kin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo kowtowed and said, "The late emperor's will forbade killing kinsmen without cause.

sentences.zh: 齊王，陛下為叔父，功高德茂，社稷重臣。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi is Your Majesty's uncle; his merit is high and his virtue abundant; he is a pillar of the state.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qi is Your Majesty's uncle; his merit and virtue are great, and he is a pillar of the realm.

sentences.zh: 陛下若無故害之，臣又順旨曲從，則臣為不忠之臣，陛下為不孝之子矣。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty should harm him without cause, and I moreover follow the intent and bend compliance, then I would be a disloyal minister and Your Majesty an unfilial son."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty harms him without cause and I go along to please you, I become a disloyal minister and Your Majesty an unfilial son."

sentences.zh: 帝不懌，由是疏之。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased; from this he grew distant from him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took offense and from then on kept his distance.

sentences.zh: 乃與開府儀同大將軍於智、鄭譯等密謀之，使智就宅候憲，因告憲有異謀。

translations.literal: He then with Grand General of the Palace Yu Zhi, Zheng Yi, and others secretly plotted; he had Zhi go to Xian's residence to wait on him and thereupon reported that Xian had a different plot.
translations.idiomatic: He then plotted in secret with Grand General of the Palace Yu Zhi, Zheng Yi, and others, sending Zhi to wait at Xian's house and accuse him of treason.

sentences.zh: 甲子，帝遣宇文孝伯語憲，欲以憲為太師，憲辭讓。

translations.literal: On jiazi the emperor sent Yuwen Xiaobo to tell Xian that he wished to make Xian Grand Preceptor; Xian declined.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the emperor sent Yuwen Xiaobo to tell Xian he meant to make him Grand Preceptor; Xian declined.

sentences.zh: 又使孝伯召憲，曰：「晚與諸王俱入。」

translations.literal: He again had Xiaobo summon Xian, saying: "Come in this evening together with the other princes."
translations.idiomatic: He again had Xiaobo summon Xian, saying, "Come in this evening with the other princes."

sentences.zh: 既至殿門，憲獨被引進。

translations.literal: When they reached the palace gate, Xian alone was led in.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the palace gate, Xian alone was brought inside.

sentences.zh: 帝先伏壯士於別室，至，即執之。

translations.literal: The emperor had first hidden strong men in a side room; when he arrived, they seized him at once.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already posted braves in a side chamber; as soon as Xian arrived, they seized him.

sentences.zh: 憲自辨理，帝使於智證憲，憲目光如炬，與智相質。

translations.literal: Xian argued his own case; the emperor had Yu Zhi testify against Xian; Xian's gaze was like torches as he confronted Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xian pleaded his own case; the emperor had Yu Zhi bear witness against him; Xian's eyes blazed as he faced Zhi down.

sentences.zh: 或謂憲曰：「以王今日事勢，何用多言！」

translations.literal: Someone said to Xian: "Given the prince's situation today, what use is much talk!"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Xian, "With your situation today, Prince, what good is more talk!"

sentences.zh: 憲曰：「死生有命，寧復圖存！

translations.literal: Xian said: "Life and death have their mandate; how could I still scheme to live!
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "Life and death are fated; I would not scheme to survive!

sentences.zh: 但老母在堂，恐留茲恨耳！」

translations.literal: Only my old mother is still in the hall; I fear to leave this regret!"
translations.idiomatic: Only that my old mother is still alive—I fear to leave her this grief!"

sentences.zh: 因擲笏於地。

translations.literal: He thereupon cast his tablet to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: With that he flung his court tablet to the floor.

sentences.zh: 遂縊之。

translations.literal: They then strangled him.
translations.idiomatic: They then strangled him.

sentences.zh: 帝召憲僚屬，使證成憲罪。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Xian's staff and made them testify to establish Xian's crime.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Xian's staff and forced them to confirm his guilt.

sentences.zh: 參軍勃海李綱，誓之以死，終無橈辭。

translations.literal: Staff adviser Li Gang of Bohai swore on his life and to the end had no bent words.
translations.idiomatic: His staff adviser Li Gang of Bohai swore he would die rather than yield, and never bent his testimony.

sentences.zh: 有司以露車載憲屍而出，故吏皆散，唯李綱撫棺號慟，躬自瘞之，哭拜而去。

translations.literal: The authorities used an open cart to carry out Xian's corpse; his former subordinates all scattered; only Li Gang stroked the coffin and wailed, personally buried him, and left weeping and bowing.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities carried Xian's body out on an open cart; his old retainers scattered, but Li Gang alone mourned over the coffin, buried him with his own hands, and left bowing and weeping.

sentences.zh: 又殺上大將軍王興、上開府儀同大將軍獨孤熊、開府儀同大將軍豆盧紹，皆素與憲親善者也。

translations.literal: He also killed Senior Grand General Wang Xing, Senior Grand General of the Palace with the same honors as the Three Excellencies Dugu Xiong, and Grand General of the Palace with the same honors as the Three Excellencies Doulu Shao—all who had long been close to Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He also killed Senior Grand General Wang Xing, Senior Palace General Dugu Xiong, and Palace General Doulu Shao—all men who had been close to Xian.

sentences.zh: 帝既誅憲而無名，乃雲與興等謀反，時人謂之「伴死」。

translations.literal: The emperor, having executed Xian without a name, then said they had plotted rebellion with Xing and the others; people of the time called it "dying in company."
translations.idiomatic: Having killed Xian without a proper charge, the emperor claimed that he and Xing and the others had plotted rebellion; contemporaries called it "tagged along in death."

sentences.zh: 以于智為柱國，封齊公，以賞之。

translations.literal: He made Yu Zhi a pillar of state and enfeoffed him as Duke of Qi, to reward him.
translations.idiomatic: He made Yu Zhi a pillar of state, enfeoffed him as Duke of Qi, and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 16閏月，乙亥，周主立妃楊氏為皇后。

translations.literal: 16. In the intercalary month, on yihai, the Zhou emperor installed consort Yang as empress.
translations.idiomatic: 16. In the intercalary month, on yihai, the Zhou emperor made Lady Yang empress.

sentences.zh: 17辛巳，周以趙王招為太師，陳王純為太傅。

translations.literal: 17. On xinsi Zhou made Prince Zhao of Zhao Grand Preceptor and Prince Chun of Chen Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: 17. On xinsi Zhou appointed Prince Zhao of Zhao Grand Preceptor and Prince Chun of Chen Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 18齊范陽王紹義聞周高祖殂，以為得天助。

translations.literal: 18. Prince Shaoyi of Fanyang of Qi, hearing that Zhou Gaozu had died, thought Heaven had aided him.
translations.idiomatic: 18. Gao Shaoyi, Prince of Fanyang of Qi, heard that Zhou Gaozu had died and took it as Heaven's help.

sentences.zh: 幽州人盧昌期，起兵據范陽，迎紹義，紹義引突厥兵赴之。

translations.literal: Lu Changqi of Youzhou raised troops and seized Fanyang to welcome Shaoyi; Shaoyi led Turkic troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Changqi of Youzhou rose in arms, seized Fanyang, and welcomed Shaoyi, who brought Turkic forces to his aid.

sentences.zh: 周遣柱國東平公神舉將兵討昌期。

translations.literal: Zhou sent the pillar of state Duke Shenju of Dongping with troops to attack Changqi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou sent the pillar of state Shenju, Duke of Dongping, with an army against Changqi.

sentences.zh: 紹義聞幽州總管出兵在外，欲乘虛襲薊，神舉遣大將軍宇文恩將四千人救之，半為紹義所殺。

translations.literal: Shaoyi heard the Youzhou regional commander had led troops out and wished to strike Ji while he was empty; Shenju sent Grand General Yuwen En with four thousand men to rescue it; half were killed by Shaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyi heard the Youzhou commander was away with his army and meant to strike Ji while it was undefended; Shenju sent Grand General Yuwen En with four thousand men to relieve it, and Shaoyi killed half of them.

sentences.zh: 會神舉克范陽，擒昌期。

translations.literal: Just then Shenju took Fanyang and captured Changqi.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Shenju took Fanyang and captured Changqi.

sentences.zh: 紹義聞之，素衣舉哀，還入突厥。

translations.literal: When Shaoyi heard it, he wore white and mourned, and returned into the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoyi heard, he put on mourning white and fled back to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 高寶寧帥夷、夏數萬騎救范陽，至潞水，聞昌期死，還，據和龍。

translations.literal: Gao Baoning led several tens of thousands of Yi and Xia cavalry to rescue Fanyang; reaching Lushui, he heard Changqi was dead, turned back, and held Helong.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Baoning led tens of thousands of Yi and Xia horsemen to relieve Fanyang; at Lushui he learned Changqi was dead, turned back, and seized Helong.

sentences.zh: 19秋，七月，周主享太廟；

translations.literal: 19. In autumn, the seventh month, the Zhou emperor offered at the Grand Temple;
translations.idiomatic: 19. In autumn, the seventh month, the Zhou emperor sacrificed at the Grand Temple;

sentences.zh: 丙午，祀圜丘。

translations.literal: on bingwu he sacrificed at the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: on bingwu he sacrificed at the Round Mound.

sentences.zh: 20庚戌，周以小宗伯斛斯征為大宗伯。

translations.literal: 20. On gengxu Zhou made Junior Director of the Ancestral Temple Husi Zheng Grand Director of the Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: 20. On gengxu Zhou made Junior Director of the Ancestral Temple Husi Zheng Grand Director of the Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以亳州總管楊堅為上柱國、大司馬。

translations.literal: On renxu he made Bozhou regional commander Yang Jian a supreme pillar of state and Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu he made Bozhou regional commander Yang Jian supreme pillar of state and Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 21癸亥，周主尊所生母李氏為帝太后。

translations.literal: 21. On guihai the Zhou emperor honored his birth mother Lady Li as Empress Dowager of the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: 21. On guihai the Zhou emperor honored his birth mother Lady Li as Empress Dowager of the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 22八月，丙寅，周主祀西郊；

translations.literal: 22. In the eighth month, on bingyin, the Zhou emperor sacrificed at the western suburb;
translations.idiomatic: 22. In the eighth month, on bingyin, the Zhou emperor sacrificed at the western suburb;

sentences.zh: 壬申，如同州。

translations.literal: on renshen he went to Tongzhou as before.
translations.idiomatic: on renshen he went to Tongzhou as before.

sentences.zh: 以大司徒杞公亮為安州總管，上柱國長孫覽為大司徒，楊公王誼為大司空。

translations.literal: He made Duke Liang of Qi, Duke of the State of Qi, Anzhou regional commander; supreme pillar of state Zhangsun Lan Grand Chamberlain; Duke Wang Yi of Yang Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He made Duke Liang of Qi regional commander of Anzhou, supreme pillar Zhangsun Lan Grand Chamberlain, and Duke Wang Yi of Yang Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以永昌公椿為大司寇。

translations.literal: On bingxu he made Duke Chun of Yongchang Grand Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu he made Duke Chun of Yongchang Grand Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 23九月，乙巳，立方明壇於婁湖。

translations.literal: 23. In the ninth month, on yisi, he established the Bright Square altar at Lou Lake.
translations.idiomatic: 23. In the ninth month, on yisi, the Bright Square altar was erected at Lou Lake.

sentences.zh: 戊申，以揚州刺史始興王叔陵為王官伯，臨盟百官。

translations.literal: On wushen he made Prince Shuling of Shixing, Yangzhou regional inspector, king-official chief and overseer of the oath before the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Prince Shuling of Shixing, Yangzhou regional inspector, was made king-official chief to preside over the oath before all officials.

sentences.zh: 24庚戌，周主封其弟元為荊王。

translations.literal: 24. On gengxu the Zhou emperor enfeoffed his younger brother Yuan as Prince of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: 24. On gengxu the Zhou emperor enfeoffed his younger brother Yuan as Prince of Jing.

sentences.zh: 25周主詔：「諸應拜者，皆以三拜成禮。」

translations.literal: 25. The Zhou emperor decreed: "All who should bow shall complete the rite with three bows."
translations.idiomatic: 25. The Zhou emperor decreed: "All who should bow shall complete the rite with three bows."

sentences.zh: 26甲寅，上幸婁湖誓眾。

translations.literal: 26. On jiayin the emperor went in person to Lou Lake to swear the host.
translations.idiomatic: 26. On jiayin the Chen emperor went in person to Lou Lake to swear in the host.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，分遣大使以盟誓班下四方，上下相警戒。

translations.literal: On yimao he separately dispatched great envoys to circulate the oath down to the four quarters, so high and low might warn one another.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao he sent great envoys in every direction to publish the oath, so court and country alike might hold one another to it.

sentences.zh: 27冬，十月，癸酉，周主還長安。

translations.literal: 27. In winter, the tenth month, on guiyou, the Zhou emperor returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: 27. In winter, the tenth month, on guiyou, the Zhou emperor returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 以大司空王誼為襄州總管。

translations.literal: He made Grand Minister of Works Wang Yi Xiangzhou regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: He made Grand Minister of Works Wang Yi regional commander of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 戊子，以尚書左僕射陸繕為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: On wuzi he made Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Lu Chan Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi he made Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat Lu Chan Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 28十一月，突厥寇周邊，圍酒泉，殺掠吏民。

translations.literal: 28. In the eleventh month the Turks raided Zhou's borders, besieged Jiuquan, and killed and plundered officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: 28. In the eleventh month the Turks raided Zhou's frontier, besieged Jiuquan, and killed and plundered officials and civilians.

sentences.zh: 29十二月，甲子，周以畢王賢為大司空。

translations.literal: 29. In the twelfth month, on jiazi, Zhou made Prince Xian of Bi Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: 29. In the twelfth month, on jiazi, Zhou made Prince Xian of Bi Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 30己丑，周以河陽總管滕王逌為行軍元帥，帥眾入寇。

translations.literal: 30. On jichou Zhou made Heyang regional commander Prince You of Teng commander-in-chief of the campaign army and led the host in invasion.
translations.idiomatic: 30. On jichou Zhou made Heyang regional commander Prince You of Teng commander-in-chief of the expeditionary army and led a force in invasion.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，癸巳，周主受朝於露門，始與群臣服漢、魏衣冠；

translations.literal: 1. In spring, the first month, on guisi, the Zhou emperor received court at the Dew Gate and for the first time he and the ministers wore Han and Wei caps and robes;
translations.idiomatic: 1. In spring, the first month, on guisi, the Zhou emperor held court at the Dew Gate and for the first time he and his ministers wore Han and Wei dress;

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元大成。

translations.literal: a general amnesty; the era name was changed to Dacheng.
translations.idiomatic: he proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Dacheng.

sentences.zh: 置四輔官：以大塚宰越王盛為大前疑，相州總管蜀公尉遲迥為大右弼，申公李穆為大左輔，大司馬隨公楊堅為大後承。

translations.literal: He established four assistant offices: he made Grand Steward Prince Sheng of Yue Grand Former Doubt, Xiangzhou regional commander Duke Chi of Shu Yuchi Jiong Grand Right Assistant, Duke Li of Shen Li Mu Grand Left Assistant, and Grand Marshal Duke Sui of Sui Yang Jian Grand Rear Bearer.
translations.idiomatic: He created four assistant posts: Grand Steward Prince Sheng of Yue became Grand Former Doubt, Xiangzhou commander Duke Jiong of Shu Yuchi Jiong Grand Right Assistant, Duke Li of Shen Li Mu Grand Left Assistant, and Grand Marshal Duke Jian of Sui Yang Jian Grand Rear Bearer.

sentences.zh: 周主之初立也，以高祖《刑書要制》為太重而除之，又數行赦宥。

translations.literal: When the Zhou emperor had first taken the throne, he held Gaozu's Essential Penal Code too heavy and abolished it, and again and again granted amnesties.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou emperor had first come to the throne, he found Gaozu's Essential Penal Statutes too harsh and repealed them, and he granted amnesties again and again.

sentences.zh: 京兆郡丞樂運上疏，以為：「《虞書》所稱『眚災肆赦』，謂過誤為害，當緩赦之。

translations.literal: Yue Yun, assistant magistrate of Jingzhao, submitted a memorial, holding: "The Documents of Yu speaks of 'disaster from error, therefore pardon,' meaning harm from mistakes should be pardoned with leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Yun of Jingzhao memorialized that "the Documents of Yu speaks of 'pardoning errors that bring disaster,' meaning harm done by mistake should be pardoned leniently.

sentences.zh: 《呂刑》云：『五刑之疑有赦。』

translations.literal: The Punishments of Lü says: 'When the five punishments are in doubt, there is pardon.'
translations.idiomatic: The Punishments of Lü says, 'When the five punishments are in doubt, pardon.'

sentences.zh: 謂刑疑從罰，罰疑從免也。

translations.literal: This means when punishment is doubtful follow penalty; when penalty is doubtful follow exemption.
translations.idiomatic: That means when punishment is doubtful, apply penalty; when penalty is doubtful, grant exemption.

sentences.zh: 謹尋經典，未有罪無輕重，溥天大赦之文。

translations.literal: Carefully searching the classics, there is no text of universal great pardon without regard to guilt light or heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Searching the classics carefully, one finds no passage of blanket amnesty without regard to the gravity of the crime.

sentences.zh: 大尊豈可數施非常之惠，以肆奸宄之惡乎！」

translations.literal: How can the Grand Lord repeatedly bestow extraordinary favor to unleash the evil of traitors and villains!"
translations.idiomatic: How can the Grand Lord repeatedly grant extraordinary favors and thereby unleash the wickedness of traitors and villains!"

sentences.zh: 帝不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 既而民輕犯法，又自以奢淫多過失，惡人規諫，欲為威虐，懾服群下。

translations.literal: Before long the people treated the law lightly; he also himself had many faults of extravagance and debauchery, hated men's remonstrance, wished to be fierce and cruel, and awe the host below.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the people held the law cheap; he himself was given to extravagance and excess, hated criticism, and sought to cow his subjects with cruelty.

sentences.zh: 乃更為《刑經聖制》，用法益深，大醮於正武殿，告天而行之。

translations.literal: He then again made the Sacred Penal Canon, using the law ever deeper; he held a great religious assembly in the Hall of Correct Martial and announced it to Heaven as he carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: He then promulgated a new Sacred Penal Canon with harsher penalties, held a great oath ceremony in the Hall of Correct Martial, and proclaimed it to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 密令左右伺察群臣，小有過失，輒行誅譴。

translations.literal: He secretly ordered attendants left and right to watch the ministers; for small faults he at once executed or reprimanded.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly ordered his attendants to spy on the ministers; the slightest fault brought execution or punishment.

sentences.zh: 又，居喪才逾年，即恣聲樂，魚龍百戲，常陳殿前，累日繼夜，不知休息；

translations.literal: Moreover, in mourning barely over a year, he at once indulged music and sound; fish-and-dragon hundred plays were constantly arrayed before the hall, days on end through the night without knowing rest;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, barely a year into mourning he gave himself over to music; fish-and-dragon entertainments and a hundred acts filled the hall day after day, night after night, without rest;

sentences.zh: 多聚美女以實後宮，增置位號，不可詳錄。

translations.literal: he gathered many beautiful women to fill the rear palace and increased posts and titles beyond detailed record.
translations.idiomatic: he packed the rear palace with beautiful women and added ranks and titles too many to list.

sentences.zh: 游宴沉湎，或旬日不出，群臣請事者，皆因宦者奏之。

translations.literal: He sank in tours and feasts; sometimes for ten days he did not emerge; ministers who requested audience all had matters reported through eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: He drowned himself in feasts and outings and sometimes did not leave the palace for ten days; any minister with business had to reach him through eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 於是樂運輿櫬詣朝堂，陳帝八失：其一，以為「大尊比來事多獨斷，不參諸宰輔，與眾共之」。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yue Yun came with his coffin to the court hall and presented the emperor's eight faults: the first, he held that "the Grand Lord of late has many matters decided alone, not consulting the chief ministers, not sharing with the host."
translations.idiomatic: Then Yue Yun came to court carrying his coffin and laid out the emperor's eight faults: first, that "the Grand Lord of late decides too much alone, without consulting the chief ministers or sharing rule with the court."

sentences.zh: 其二，「搜美女以實後宮，儀同以上女不許輒嫁，貴賤同怨」。

translations.literal: The second, "searching beautiful women to fill the rear palace; women of officials of the third rank and above may not marry at will—the noble and base alike resent it."
translations.idiomatic: Second, "he hunts beautiful women for the rear palace and forbids daughters of officials of the third rank and above to marry at will, so high and low alike resent it."

sentences.zh: 其三，「大尊一入後宮，數日不出，所須聞奏，多附宦者」。

translations.literal: The third, "once the Grand Lord enters the rear palace, for many days he does not emerge; what must be heard in memorial comes mostly through eunuchs."
translations.idiomatic: Third, "once the Grand Lord enters the rear palace he stays for days; business that should reach him mostly goes through eunuchs."

sentences.zh: 其四，「下詔寬刑，未及半年，更嚴前制」。

translations.literal: The fourth, "he issued an edict to lighten punishments, but before half a year he was stricter than the former system."
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, "he issued an edict to lighten punishments, yet before half a year had passed he was harsher than before."

sentences.zh: 其五，「高祖斫雕為樸，崩未逾年，而遽窮奢麗」。

translations.literal: The fifth, "Gaozu carved away ornament for simplicity; not yet a year since his death, and he hastens to exhaust luxury and splendor."
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, "Gaozu stripped ornament for simplicity; not a year since his death, and the Grand Lord rushes into extravagance."

sentences.zh: 其六，「徭賦下民，以奉俳優角抵」。

translations.literal: The sixth, "corvée and tax burden the people to supply actors and wrestlers."
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, "he burdens the people with corvée and taxes to feed actors and wrestlers."

sentences.zh: 其七，「上書字誤者，即治其罪，杜獻書之路」。

translations.literal: The seventh, "whoever errs in a character in a memorial is at once punished for the crime, blocking the road of presenting books."
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, "whoever makes a slip in a memorial character is punished at once, shutting the door to honest memorials."

sentences.zh: 其八，「玄象垂誡，不能咨諏善道，修布德政」。

translations.literal: The eighth, "the dark signs hang warnings, yet he cannot consult on the good Way and spread virtuous government."
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, "Heaven sends warnings in the sky, yet he will not seek good counsel or spread virtuous rule."

sentences.zh: 「若不革茲八事，臣見周廟不血食矣。」

translations.literal: "If these eight matters are not reformed, your servant sees Zhou's temple will not receive blood sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: "Unless these eight are corrected, I see Zhou's ancestral temple receiving no sacrifices."

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，將殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and was about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and was about to execute him.

sentences.zh: 朝臣恐懼，莫有救者。

translations.literal: The court ministers were afraid; none rescued him.
translations.idiomatic: The court was terrified; no one dared speak for him.

sentences.zh: 內史中大夫洛陽元巖漢曰：「臧洪同死，人猶願之，況比干乎！

translations.literal: Grand Master of the Palace Secretariat Yuan Yan of Luoyang said: "When Zang Hong died together with others, men still wished it; how much more Bi Gan!
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of the Palace Secretariat Yuan Yan of Luoyang said, "When Zang Hong chose death with his lord, men still admired him; how much more Bi Gan!

sentences.zh: 若樂運不免，吾將與之俱斃。」

translations.literal: If Yue Yun is not spared, I shall die with him."
translations.idiomatic: If Yue Yun is not spared, I mean to die with him."

sentences.zh: 乃詣閣請見，曰：「樂運不顧其死，欲以求名。

translations.literal: He then went to the gate to request audience, saying: "Yue Yun does not care for his life, wishing to seek a name.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the gate and asked to see the emperor, saying, "Yue Yun courts death to win a name.

sentences.zh: 陛下不如勞而遣之，以廣聖度。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty would do better to honor his effort and send him away, to broaden sagely measure."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty would do better to spare him with honor and let him go, and so show your magnanimity."

sentences.zh: 帝頗感悟。

translations.literal: The emperor was quite moved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 明日，召運，謂曰：「朕昨夜思卿所奏，實為忠臣。」

translations.literal: The next day he summoned Yun and said to him, "Last night I reflected on your memorial; you are truly a loyal minister."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he summoned Yue Yun and said, "I spent last night thinking over what you submitted; you are a true loyal minister."

sentences.zh: 賜御食而罷之。

translations.literal: He bestowed imperial food upon him and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him food from the imperial table and let him go.

sentences.zh: 2癸卯，周立皇子闡為魯王。

translations.literal: 2. On guimao the Zhou established Prince Chan as King of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: 2. On guimao Zhou invested Prince Chan as King of Lu.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，周主東巡；

translations.literal: On jiachen the Zhou ruler made an eastern tour;
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the Zhou emperor set out on an eastern tour;

sentences.zh: 丙午，以許公宇文善為大宗伯。

translations.literal: on bingwu he appointed Duke of Xu Yuwen Shan Grand Minister of Protocol.
translations.idiomatic: on bingwu he made Duke of Xu Yuwen Shan Grand Minister of Protocol.

sentences.zh: 戊午，周主至洛陽；

translations.literal: On wuwu the Zhou ruler reached Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu the Zhou emperor arrived at Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 立魯王闡為皇太子。

translations.literal: he established King of Lu Chan as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: he invested King of Lu Chan as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 3二月，癸亥，上耕藉田。

translations.literal: 3. In the second month, on guihai, the emperor ploughed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: 3. In the second month, on guihai, the emperor performed the ploughing ceremony in the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 4周下詔，以洛陽為東京；

translations.literal: 4. Zhou issued an edict making Luoyang the Eastern Capital;
translations.idiomatic: 4. Zhou issued an edict designating Luoyang as the Eastern Capital;

sentences.zh: 發山東諸州兵治洛陽宮，常役四萬人。

translations.literal: it mobilized troops from the eastern provinces to repair the Luoyang palace, with forty thousand men on permanent corvée.
translations.idiomatic: it called up soldiers from the eastern provinces to rebuild the Luoyang palace, keeping forty thousand men on standing corvée.

sentences.zh: 徒相州六府於洛陽。

translations.literal: It moved the six offices of Xiangzhou to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: It transferred the six offices of Xiangzhou to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 5周徐州總管王軌，聞鄭譯用事，自知及禍，謂所親曰：「吾昔在先朝，實申社稷至計。

translations.literal: 5. Zhou Xuzhou regional commander Wang Gui, hearing that Zheng Yi held power, knew disaster would reach him and said to those close to him, "In the former reign I truly set forth the utmost plans for altar and state.
translations.idiomatic: 5. Zhou Xuzhou regional commander Wang Gui, learning that Zheng Yi was in charge, knew his end was near and told his intimates, "Under the late emperor I spoke the deepest plans for the realm's survival.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，斷可知矣。

translations.literal: Today's affair can be known for certain in advance.
translations.idiomatic: What is happening now was easy to foresee.

sentences.zh: 此州控帶淮南，鄰接強寇，欲為身計，易如反掌。

translations.literal: This province controls the Huai region and borders a powerful foe; to plot for one's own person would be as easy as turning the hand.
translations.idiomatic: This province commands the Huai and lies next to a strong enemy; if I schemed for myself, it would be easy as turning my hand.

sentences.zh: 但忠義之節，不可虧違，況荷先帝厚恩，豈可以獲罪於嗣主，遽忘之邪！

translations.literal: Yet the integrity of loyalty and righteousness cannot be impaired; moreover, having received the late emperor's deep grace, how could one forget it and earn guilt from the succeeding lord!
translations.idiomatic: But loyalty and righteousness cannot be bent; and having received the late emperor's great favor, how could I forget it and offend his heir!

sentences.zh: 正可於此待死，冀千載之後，知吾此心耳！」

translations.literal: One can only await death here, hoping that a thousand years hence men will know this heart of mine!"
translations.idiomatic: I can only wait here for death, in the hope that a thousand years from now men will know what I meant!"

sentences.zh: 周主從容問譯曰：「我腳杖痕，誰所為也？」

translations.literal: The Zhou ruler asked Zheng Yi at ease, "The cane marks on my feet—who made them?"
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou emperor casually asked Zheng Yi, "Who gave me these cane marks on my feet?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「事由烏丸軌、宇文孝伯。」

translations.literal: He replied, "The matter arose from Wuhuan Gui and Yuwen Xiaobo."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "It came from Wuhuan Gui and Yuwen Xiaobo."

sentences.zh: 因言軌捋鬚事。

translations.literal: He then spoke of Gui's seizing his beard.
translations.idiomatic: He then brought up how Gui had grabbed his beard.

sentences.zh: 帝使內史杜慶信就州殺軌，元巖不肯署詔。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Palace Secretariat officer Du Qingxin to the province to kill Gui; Yuan Yan refused to countersign the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Palace Secretariat officer Du Qingxin to the province to execute Gui; Yuan Yan would not sign the edict.

sentences.zh: 御正中大夫顏之儀切諫，帝不聽，巖進繼之，脫巾頓顙，三拜三進。

translations.literal: Chief Master of the Imperial Rectifier Yan Zhiyi remonstrated sharply; the emperor would not listen, and Yan advanced in succession, doffing his cap and knocking his forehead, thrice bowing and thrice advancing.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Master of the Imperial Rectifier Yan Zhiyi argued fiercely; the emperor would not heed him, and Yan pressed forward, removing his cap and striking his brow, bowing three times and advancing three times.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「汝欲黨烏丸軌邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Do you wish to shield Wuhuan Gui?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Do you mean to shield Wuhuan Gui?"

sentences.zh: 巖曰：「臣非黨軌，正恐濫誅失天下之望。」

translations.literal: Yan said, "Your servant is not shielding Gui; I only fear that indiscriminate killing will lose the empire's hopes."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yan said, "I am not shielding Gui; I fear that killing without cause will cost you the world's trust."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，使閹豎搏其面。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged and had eunuchs strike his face.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and had eunuchs beat his face.

sentences.zh: 軌遂死，巖亦廢於家。

translations.literal: Gui then died, and Yan was also dismissed to his home.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was put to death, and Yuan Yan was sent home in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 遠近知與不知，皆為軌流涕。

translations.literal: Near and far, whether they knew him or not, all wept for Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far, all who knew him and all who did not wept for Gui.

sentences.zh: 之儀，之推之弟也。

translations.literal: Zhiyi was the younger brother of Zhi Tui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi was the younger brother of Yan Zhi Tui.

sentences.zh: 周主之為太子也，上柱國尉遲運為宮正，數進諫，不用；

translations.literal: When the Zhou ruler had been crown prince, Senior Pillar of State Yuchi Yun was director of the palace establishment and repeatedly offered remonstrance, but was not heeded;
translations.idiomatic: While the Zhou heir apparent was still crown prince, Senior Pillar of State Yuchi Yun had been director of the palace establishment and often remonstrated, without effect;

sentences.zh: 又與王軌、宇文孝伯、宇文神舉皆為高祖所親待，太子疑其同毀己。

translations.literal: he, together with Wang Gui, Yuwen Xiaobo, and Yuwen Shenju, were all treated with intimacy by Gaozu, and the crown prince suspected they jointly slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: he, Wang Gui, Yuwen Xiaobo, and Yuwen Shenju had all been favored by Gaozu, and the crown prince suspected they were plotting together to ruin him.

sentences.zh: 及軌死，運懼，私謂孝伯曰：「吾徒必不免禍，為之奈何？」

translations.literal: When Gui died, Yun was afraid and privately said to Xiaobo, "Our party is sure not to escape disaster—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: After Gui died, Yun was terrified and said privately to Xiaobo, "Our group cannot escape calamity—what can we do?"

sentences.zh: 孝伯曰：「今堂上有老母，地下有武帝。

translations.literal: Xiaobo said, "Now above the hall there is an aged mother; below the earth there is Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "Above, there is an old mother in the hall; below, there is Emperor Wu in his tomb.

sentences.zh: 為臣為子，知欲何之！

translations.literal: As minister and as son, one knows where one should go!
translations.idiomatic: As subject and as son, you know where you must go!

sentences.zh: 且委質事人，本徇名義；

translations.literal: Moreover, having entrusted one's person to serve another, one originally pursues name and righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: Besides, we pledged ourselves to serve him for honor's sake;

sentences.zh: 諫而不入，死焉可逃！

translations.literal: if remonstrance is not accepted, how can death be escaped!
translations.idiomatic: if he will not heed counsel, death is the only escape!

sentences.zh: 足下若為身計，宜且遠之。」

translations.literal: If you plot for your own person, you should for the time being keep your distance."
translations.idiomatic: If you are scheming for yourself, you had better keep away for now."

sentences.zh: 於是運求出為秦州總管。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yun requested assignment as Qinzhou regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Yun then asked to be sent out as Qinzhou regional commander.

sentences.zh: 他日，帝托以齊王憲事讓孝伯曰：「公知齊王謀反，何以不言？」

translations.literal: Another day the emperor, using Prince Xian of Qi's affair as a pretext, reproached Xiaobo, saying, "You knew Prince Xian of Qi was plotting rebellion—why did you not speak?"
translations.idiomatic: On another day the emperor, using the case of Prince Xian of Qi as a pretext, reproached Xiaobo: "You knew the Prince of Qi was plotting rebellion—why did you not speak?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣知齊王忠於社稷，為群小所譖，言必不用，所以不言。

translations.literal: He replied, "Your servant knew Prince Xian of Qi was loyal to altar and state and was slandered by petty men; if he spoke it would surely not be used—therefore he did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I knew the Prince of Qi was loyal to the dynasty and was maligned by petty men; I knew my words would not be heeded, so I kept silent.

sentences.zh: 且先帝付囑微臣，唯令輔導陛下。

translations.literal: Moreover the late emperor entrusted your servant, charging him only to assist and guide Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the late emperor entrusted me only to assist and guide Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 今諫而不從，實負顧托。

translations.literal: Now remonstrance is not followed—this truly fails the entrustment.
translations.idiomatic: Now that you will not heed counsel, I have failed that charge.

sentences.zh: 以此為罪，是所甘心。」

translations.literal: To take this as crime is what the heart is willing for."
translations.idiomatic: If that is my crime, I accept it gladly."

sentences.zh: 帝大慚，俯首不語，命將出，賜死於家。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly ashamed, bowed his head and said nothing, ordered him taken out, and bestowed death at home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply shamed, bowed his head in silence, ordered him taken out, and had him die at home by imperial gift.

sentences.zh: 時宇文神舉為并州刺史，帝遣使就州鴆殺之。

translations.literal: At that time Yuwen Shenju was Bingzhou regional commander; the emperor sent an envoy to the province to kill him with poisoned wine.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shenju was then regional commander of Bingzhou; the emperor sent an envoy to the province to kill him with poisoned wine.

sentences.zh: 尉遲運至秦州，亦以憂死。

translations.literal: Yuchi Yun reached Qinzhou and also died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Yun reached Qinzhou and likewise died of grief.

sentences.zh: 6周罷南伐諸軍。

translations.literal: 6. Zhou disbanded the armies for the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: 6. Zhou stood down the armies for the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 突厥佗缽可汗請和於周，周主以趙王招女為千金公主，妻之，且命執送高紹義；

translations.literal: The Tujue Tabo Khan requested peace with Zhou; the Zhou ruler took the daughter of Prince Zhao Zhao as Princess Qianjin, married her to him, and also ordered him to seize and deliver Gao Shaoyi;
translations.idiomatic: The Tujue khan Tabo asked Zhou for peace; the Zhou emperor gave Prince Zhao Zhao's daughter as Princess Qianjin in marriage and also ordered Tabo to seize and hand over Gao Shaoyi;

sentences.zh: 佗缽不從。

translations.literal: Tabo did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Tabo refused.

sentences.zh: 7辛巳，周宣帝傳位於太子闡，大赦，改元大象，自稱天元皇帝，所居稱「天台」，冕二十四旒，車服旗鼓皆倍於前王之數。

translations.literal: 7. On xinsi Emperor Xuān of Zhou transmitted the throne to Crown Prince Chan, proclaimed a great amnesty, changed the era name to Great Elephant, styled himself Lord of Heaven Emperor, called his residence "Terrace of Heaven," wore a cap with twenty-four tassels, and doubled the number of his chariots, robes, banners, and drums over former kings.
translations.idiomatic: 7. On xinsi Emperor Xuān of Zhou abdicated to Crown Prince Chan, declared a general amnesty, changed the era name to Great Elephant, styled himself Lord of Heaven Emperor, named his residence the Terrace of Heaven, took a twenty-four-tassel crown, and doubled every count of chariots, robes, banners, and drums that former kings had used.

sentences.zh: 皇帝稱正陽宮，置納言、御正、諸衛等官，皆准天台。

translations.literal: The emperor was styled the Zhengyang Palace, with offices such as Counselor-in-Chief, Imperial Rectifier, and the various guards, all modeled on the Terrace of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The reigning emperor was lodged at the Zhengyang Palace, with posts such as Counselor-in-Chief, Imperial Rectifier, and the various guards, all patterned on the Terrace of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 尊皇太后為天元皇太后。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was honored as Lord of Heaven Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was elevated to Lord of Heaven Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 天元既傳位，驕侈彌甚，務自尊大，無所顧憚，國之儀典，率情變更。

translations.literal: Once Lord Yuan had transmitted the throne, his arrogance and extravagance grew still greater; he strove to magnify himself and feared nothing, altering the state's ritual codes as whim dictated.
translations.idiomatic: After Lord Yuan had abdicated, his arrogance and extravagance only grew; he insisted on his own grandeur and shrank from nothing, changing the state's ritual codes on impulse.

sentences.zh: 每對臣下自稱為天、用樽、彝、珪、瓚以飲食。

translations.literal: Facing his ministers he called himself Heaven and used zun, yi, gui, and zan vessels for food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: Before his ministers he called himself Heaven and ate and drank from ritual vessels reserved for the sacred—zun, yi, gui, and zan.

sentences.zh: 令群臣朝天台者，致齋三日，清身一日。

translations.literal: He ordered that ministers who attended the Terrace of Heaven fast for three days and purify the body for one day.
translations.idiomatic: He required ministers who attended the Terrace of Heaven to fast three days and purify themselves for one day.

sentences.zh: 既自比上帝，不欲群臣同己，常自帶綬，及冠通天冠，加金附蟬，顧見侍臣弁上有金蟬及王公有綬者，並令去之。

translations.literal: Comparing himself to the Supreme Lord, he did not wish ministers to be his equals; he always wore the sash himself and, on the Through-Heaven cap, added gold with the cicada ornament; seeing attendants with cicadas on their caps or kings and dukes wearing sashes, he ordered them all removed.
translations.idiomatic: Having likened himself to God, he would not let ministers match him: he always wore the ceremonial sash himself, and on his Through-Heaven cap added a gold cicada ornament; whenever he noticed attendants with cicadas on their caps or kings and dukes wearing sashes, he had them removed.

sentences.zh: 不聽人有「天」、「高」、「上」、「大」之稱，官名有犯，皆改之。

translations.literal: He forbade others to use the words "Heaven," "high," "upper," or "great"; any official title that violated this was changed.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade anyone to use the words heaven, high, upper, or great; any office title that infringed was changed.

sentences.zh: 改姓高者為「姜」，九族稱高祖者為「長祖」。

translations.literal: Those surnamed Gao were changed to "Jiang"; the nine clans' title for Gaozu was changed to "Chief Ancestor."
translations.idiomatic: He changed the surname Gao to Jiang, and the nine clans' term for Gaozu to Chief Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 又令天下車皆以渾木為輪。

translations.literal: He also ordered that all chariots in the empire use solid wooden wheels.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered every cart in the realm to use solid wooden wheels.

sentences.zh: 禁天下婦人不得施粉黛，自非宮人，皆黃眉墨汝。

translations.literal: He forbade women throughout the empire to apply powder and rouge; except for palace women, all were to have yellow brows and black cosmetic paint.
translations.idiomatic: He banned women throughout the realm from using powder and rouge; except for palace women, all were to paint their brows yellow and black.

sentences.zh: 每召侍臣論議，唯欲興造變革，未嘗言及政事。

translations.literal: Whenever he summoned attending ministers to discuss affairs, he wished only to launch works and reforms and never spoke of government.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he called ministers in to discuss affairs, he talked only of new projects and reforms, never of government.

sentences.zh: 遊戲無常，出入不節，羽儀仗衛，晨出夜還，陪侍之官，皆不堪命。

translations.literal: His diversions had no fixed pattern and his comings and goings had no rule; with insignia and guards he set out at dawn and returned at night, and the officials who accompanied him could not endure it.
translations.idiomatic: His amusements had no fixed pattern and his comings and goings no schedule; with full guard he would leave at dawn and return at night, and the officials who attended him were driven past endurance.

sentences.zh: 自公卿以下，常被楚撻。

translations.literal: From the Three Dukes down, they were constantly beaten with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: From the Three Dukes downward, men were constantly beaten with the staff.

sentences.zh: 每捶人，皆以百二十為度，謂之「天杖」，其後又加至二百四十。

translations.literal: Whenever he beat someone, the count was always one hundred twenty strokes, called the "Staff of Heaven"; later it was increased to two hundred forty.
translations.idiomatic: Each beating ran to one hundred twenty strokes, called the Staff of Heaven; later he raised it to two hundred forty.

sentences.zh: 宮人內職亦如之，後、妃、嬪、御，雖被寵幸，亦多杖背。

translations.literal: Palace women and inner offices were treated the same; empresses, consorts, concubines, and attendants—even when favored—often had their backs beaten.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women and inner staff fared the same; empresses, consorts, concubines, and attendants—even when favored—were often beaten on the back.

sentences.zh: 於是內外恐怖，人不自安，皆求苟免，莫有固志，重足累息，以逮於終。

translations.literal: Thereupon inside and outside were terrified; men could not be at ease; all sought to escape by any means and none held firm purpose; with doubled feet and piled breaths they reached the end.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside the court were terrified; no one felt safe; all sought any escape and none stood firm; they went in fear, holding their breath, until the end.

sentences.zh: 8戊子，周以越王盛為太保，尉遲迥為大前疑，代王達為大右弼。

translations.literal: 8. On wuzi Zhou appointed Prince Yue Sheng as Grand Preceptor, Yuchi Jiong as Grand Mentor of the First Rank, and Prince Dai Da as Grand Assistant of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: 8. On wuzi Zhou made Prince Yue Sheng Grand Preceptor, Yuchi Jiong Grand Mentor of the First Rank, and Prince Dai Da Grand Assistant of the Right.

sentences.zh: 9辛卯，徙鄴城《石經》於洛陽。

translations.literal: 9. On xinmao the Stone Classics of Ye were moved to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: 9. On xinmao the Stone Classics of Ye were transferred to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 詔：「河陽、幽、相、豫、亳、青、徐七總管，並受東京六府處分。」

translations.literal: An edict said, "The seven regional commands of Heyang, You, Xiang, Yu, Bo, Qing, and Xu shall all receive orders from the six offices of the Eastern Capital."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared, "The seven regional commands of Heyang, You, Xiang, Yu, Bo, Qing, and Xu shall all take orders from the six offices of the Eastern Capital."

sentences.zh: 10三月，庚申，天元還長安，大陳軍伍，親擐甲冑，入自青門，靜帝備法駕以從。

translations.literal: 10. In the third month, on gengshen, Lord Yuan returned to Chang'an, arrayed the army in great formation, donned armor himself, entered by the Green Gate, and Emperor Jing prepared the full imperial equipage to follow.
translations.idiomatic: 10. In the third month, on gengshen, Lord Yuan returned to Chang'an, paraded the troops in force, buckled on armor himself, entered through the Green Gate, and Emperor Jing rode behind in full imperial state.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬戌朔，立妃朱氏為天元帝后。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on the first day of the month (renxu), he established Consort Zhu as empress of the Lord of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day of the month (renxu), he made Consort Zhu empress to the Lord of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 后，吳人，本出寒微，生靜帝，長於天元十餘歲，疏賤無寵，以靜帝故，特尊之。

translations.literal: The empress was a man of Wu, originally of humble birth; she bore Emperor Jing and was more than ten years older than Lord Yuan, neglected and without favor, but was specially honored because of Emperor Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was a Wu native of humble origin; she had borne Emperor Jing and was more than ten years older than Lord Yuan, kept at a distance and without favor, yet honored especially for Emperor Jing's sake.

sentences.zh: 11乙巳，周主祠太廟。

translations.literal: 11. On yisi the Zhou ruler sacrificed at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: 11. On yisi the Zhou emperor sacrificed at the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 壬午，大醮於正武殿。

translations.literal: On renwu he held a great communal feast in the Hall of Correct Martial.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu he held a great communal feast in the Hall of Correct Martial.

sentences.zh: 12五月，辛亥，以襄國郡為趙國，濟南郡為陳國，武當、安富二郡為越國，上黨郡為代國，新野郡為滕國，邑各萬戶；

translations.literal: 12. In the fifth month, on xinhai, Xiangguo commandery was made the State of Zhao, Jinan commandery the State of Chen, Wudang and Anfu commanderies the State of Yue, Shangdang commandery the State of Dai, Xinye commandery the State of Teng, each with ten thousand households;
translations.idiomatic: 12. In the fifth month, on xinhai, Xiangguo commandery was made the state of Zhao, Jinan the state of Chen, Wudang and Anfu together the state of Yue, Shangdang the state of Dai, and Xinye the state of Teng, each with ten thousand households;

sentences.zh: 令趙王招、陳王純、越王盛、代王達、滕王逌並之國。

translations.literal: he ordered Princes Zhao Zhao, Chen Chun, Yue Sheng, Dai Da, and Teng You each to go to his state.
translations.idiomatic: he sent Princes Zhao Zhao, Chen Chun, Yue Sheng, Dai Da, and Teng You each to his domain.

sentences.zh: 隨公楊堅私謂大將軍汝南公慶曰：「天元實無積德；

translations.literal: Duke of Sui Yang Jian said privately to General-in-Chief Duke of Runan Qing, "Lord Yuan truly has no accumulated virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Sui Yang Jian said privately to General-in-Chief Duke of Runan Qing, "Lord Yuan has built up no real virtue;

sentences.zh: 視其相貌，壽亦不長。

translations.literal: judging by his appearance, his life will not be long either.
translations.idiomatic: to judge by his face, his life will not be long.

sentences.zh: 又，諸籓微弱，各令就國，曾無深根固本之計。

translations.literal: Moreover the various princes are weak; each is ordered to his state, with never a plan to set deep roots and secure the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the feudal princes are weak; each is sent to his state with no plan to plant deep roots or secure the foundation.

sentences.zh: 羽翮既剪，何能及遠哉！」

translations.literal: Once the wings are clipped, how can they reach far!"
translations.idiomatic: Once their wings are clipped, how far can they fly?"

sentences.zh: 慶，神舉之弟也。

translations.literal: Qing was Shenju's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was the younger brother of Shenju.

sentences.zh: 13突厥寇周并州。

translations.literal: 13. The Tujue raided Zhou's Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: 13. The Tujue raided Zhou's Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 六月，周發山東諸民修長城。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Zhou mobilized the people of the eastern provinces to repair the Long Wall.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Zhou mobilized the people of the eastern provinces to repair the Long Wall.

sentences.zh: 14秋，七月，庚寅，周以楊堅為大前疑，柱國司馬消難為大後承。

translations.literal: 14. Autumn, seventh month, on gengyin Zhou appointed Yang Jian Grand Mentor of the First Rank and Pillar of State Sima Xiaonan Grand Bearer of the Rear.
translations.idiomatic: 14. In autumn, the seventh month, on gengyin Zhou made Yang Jian Grand Mentor of the First Rank and Pillar of State Sima Xiaonan Grand Bearer of the Rear.

sentences.zh: 15辛卯，初用大貨六銖錢。

translations.literal: 15. On xinmao they first used the Great Currency six-zhu coin.
translations.idiomatic: 15. On xinmao they first issued the Great Currency six-zhu coin.

sentences.zh: 16丙申，周納司馬消難女為正陽宮皇后。

translations.literal: 16. On bingshen Zhou took Sima Xiaonan's daughter into the Zhengyang Palace as empress.
translations.idiomatic: 16. On bingshen Zhou took Sima Xiaonan's daughter into the Zhengyang Palace as empress.

sentences.zh: 己酉，周尊天元帝太后李氏為天皇太后，壬子，改天元皇后朱氏為天皇后，立妃元氏為天右皇后，陳氏為天左皇后，凡四後雲。

translations.literal: On jiyou Zhou honored Lord of Heaven Emperor's Empress Dowager Lady Li as Grand Lord of Heaven Empress Dowager; on renzi he changed Lord of Heaven Empress Zhu to Grand Empress, established Consort Yuan as Grand Empress of the Right, and Consort Chen as Grand Empress of the Left—four empresses in all.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Zhou elevated Lord of Heaven Emperor's Empress Dowager Lady Li to Grand Lord of Heaven Empress Dowager; on renzi he changed Lord of Heaven Empress Zhu to Grand Empress, made Consort Yuan Grand Empress of the Right and Consort Chen Grand Empress of the Left—four empresses in all.

sentences.zh: 元氏，開府儀同大將軍晟之女；

translations.literal: Consort Yuan was the daughter of General-in-Chief of the Palace Gate with Honored Title of Peerage Yuan Sheng;
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yuan was the daughter of General-in-Chief of the Palace Gate with Honored Title of Peerage Yuan Sheng;

sentences.zh: 陳氏，大將軍山提之女也。

translations.literal: Consort Chen was the daughter of General-in-Chief Chen Shanti.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Chen was the daughter of General-in-Chief Chen Shanti.

sentences.zh: 17八月，庚申，天元如同州。

translations.literal: 17. In the eighth month, on gengshen, Lord Yuan went to Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: 17. In the eighth month, on gengshen, Lord Yuan went to Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 18丁卯，上閱武於大壯觀。

translations.literal: 18. On dingmao the emperor reviewed troops at the Grand Martial Viewing Ground.
translations.idiomatic: 18. On dingmao the emperor reviewed troops at the Grand Martial Viewing Ground.

sentences.zh: 命都督任忠帥步騎十萬陳於玄武湖，都督陳景帥樓艦五百出瓜步江，振旅而還。

translations.literal: He ordered Commander Ren Zhong to lead one hundred thousand foot and horse in formation at Xuanwu Lake, and Commander Chen Jing to lead five hundred tower ships out on the Guazhou stretch of the Yangtze, then returned the army in array.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Commander Ren Zhong to array one hundred thousand infantry and cavalry at Xuanwu Lake, and Commander Chen Jing to lead five hundred tower ships onto the Guazhou reach of the Yangtze, then marched the force home in review.

sentences.zh: 19壬申，周天元還長安。

translations.literal: 19. On renshen Lord Yuan of Zhou returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: 19. On renshen Lord Yuan of Zhou returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以陳山提、元晟並為上柱國。

translations.literal: On jiaxu he made Chen Shanti and Yuan Sheng both Senior Pillars of State.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu he made Chen Shanti and Yuan Sheng both Senior Pillars of State.

sentences.zh: 20戊寅，上還宮。

translations.literal: 20. On wuyin the emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: 20. On wuyin the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 豫章內史南康王方泰，在郡秩滿，縱火延燒邑居，因行暴掠，驅錄富人，徵求財賄。

translations.literal: Prince Fangtai of Nankang, interior governor of Yuzhang, when his term in the commandery expired set fires that spread through the town and then went about plundering, driving off the wealthy to extort bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Fangtai of Nankang, interior governor of Yuzhang, when his term in the commandery ended set fires that burned through the town, then rampaged and plundered, driving off the rich to squeeze them for bribes.

sentences.zh: 上閱武，方泰當從，啟稱母疾不行，而微服往民間淫人妻，為州所錄。

translations.literal: When the emperor reviewed troops Fangtai should have attended; he reported that his mother was ill and could not go, yet in plain dress went among the people seducing men's wives and was seized by the province.
translations.idiomatic: At the troop review Fangtai should have attended; he reported his mother was ill and stayed away, yet in disguise went among the people seducing men's wives and was caught by the provincial authorities.

sentences.zh: 又帥人仗抗拒，傷禁司，為有司所奏。

translations.literal: He also led men with weapons to resist, wounding the prohibition officers, and was memorialized by the responsible officials.
translations.idiomatic: He also led armed men to resist, injuring the prohibition officers, and the responsible officials memorialized against him.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，下方泰獄，免官，削爵土，尋而復舊。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged, sent Fangtai to prison, removed him from office, and stripped his fief, but soon restored him as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, threw Fangtai into prison, removed him from office, and stripped his fief, but soon restored him as before.

sentences.zh: 21壬午，周以上柱國畢王賢為太師，郇公韓業為大左輔。

translations.literal: 21. On renwu Zhou appointed Supreme Pillar of State Prince Bi Xian as Grand Preceptor and Duke of Xun Han Ye as Grand Left Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: 21. On renwu Zhou appointed Supreme Pillar of State Prince Bi Xian grand preceptor and Duke of Xun Han Ye grand left assistant.

sentences.zh: 九月，乙卯，以酆王貞為大塚宰。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on yimao, Prince Feng Zhen was made Grand Steward.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on yimao, Prince Feng Zhen was made grand steward.

sentences.zh: 以鄖公韋孝寬為行軍元帥，帥行軍總管杞公亮、郕公梁士彥寇淮南。

translations.literal: Duke of Yun Wei Xiaokuan was made campaign marshal and led campaign commanders Duke of Qi Liang and Duke of Xing Liang Shiyan to raid Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Yun Wei Xiaokuan was made campaign marshal and led campaign commanders Duke of Qi Liang and Duke of Xing Liang Shiyan against Huainan.

sentences.zh: 仍遣御正杜杲、禮部薛舒來聘。

translations.literal: He also sent Imperial Rectifier Du Guo and the Ministry of Rites' Xue Shu on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent imperial rectifier Du Guo and Xue Shu of the Ministry of Rites on a friendly mission.

sentences.zh: 22冬，十月，壬戌，周天元幸道會苑，大醮，以高祖配醮。

translations.literal: 22. In winter, the tenth month, on renxu, Tianyuan of Zhou visited Daohui Park, performed a great jiao sacrifice, and paired Gaozu in the offering.
translations.idiomatic: 22. In winter, the tenth month, on renxu, Emperor Tianyuan of Zhou visited Daohui Park, performed a great jiao sacrifice, and paired Gaozu in the offering.

sentences.zh: 初復佛像及天尊像，天元與二像俱南面坐，大陳雜戲，令長安士民縱觀。

translations.literal: Buddha images and images of the Heavenly Lord were restored for the first time; Tianyuan sat facing south together with the two images, staged many entertainments, and allowed the people of Chang'an to watch freely.
translations.idiomatic: Buddha images and images of the Heavenly Lord were restored; Tianyuan sat facing south with the two images, staged many entertainments, and let the people of Chang'an watch freely.

sentences.zh: 23甲戌，以尚書僕射陸繕為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: 23. On jiaxu Lu Chan was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: 23. On jiaxu Lu Chan was made left vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 24十一月，辛卯，大赦。

translations.literal: 24. In the eleventh month, on xinmao, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: 24. In the eleventh month, on xinmao, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 25周韋孝寬分遣杞公亮自安陸攻黃城，梁士彥攻廣陵。

translations.literal: 25. Wei Xiaokuan of Zhou separately sent Duke of Qi Liang from Anlu to attack Huangcheng and Liang Shiyan to attack Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: 25. Wei Xiaokuan of Zhou sent Duke of Qi Liang from Anlu against Huangcheng and Liang Shiyan against Guangling.

sentences.zh: 甲午，士彥至肥口。

translations.literal: On jiawu Shiyan reached Feikou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Shiyan reached Feikou.

sentences.zh: 26乙未，周天元如溫湯。

translations.literal: 26. On yiwei Tianyuan of Zhou went to the hot springs.
translations.idiomatic: 26. On yiwei Emperor Tianyuan went to the hot springs.

sentences.zh: 27戊戌，周軍進圍壽陽。

translations.literal: 27. On wuxu the Zhou army advanced to besiege Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: 27. On wuxu the Zhou army advanced to besiege Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 28周天元如同州。

translations.literal: 28. Tianyuan of Zhou went to Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: 28. Emperor Tianyuan went to Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 29詔開府儀同三司、南兗州刺史淳於量為上流水軍都督，中領軍樊毅都督北討諸軍事，左衛將軍任忠都督北討前軍事，前豐州刺史皋文奏帥步騎三千趣陽平郡。

translations.literal: 29. It was decreed that General of the Open Office with Equal Honor in Three Departments and Governor of Southern Yanzhou Chunyu Liang should be commander of the upper-stream navy; Central Commander-in-Chief Fan Yi should command all northern expedition forces; Left Guard General Ren Zhong should command the vanguard of the northern expedition; and former Governor of Fengzhou Gao Wenzou should lead three thousand foot and horse toward Yangping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: 29. Chunyu Liang, general of the open office with equal honor in three departments and governor of Southern Yanzhou, was made commander of the upper-stream navy; Fan Yi, central commander-in-chief, was made commander of all northern expedition forces; Ren Zhong, left guard general, was made commander of the northern expedition vanguard; and former Fengzhou governor Gao Wenzou was to lead three thousand foot and horse toward Yangping commandery.

sentences.zh: 30壬寅，周天元還長安。

translations.literal: 30. On renyin Tianyuan of Zhou returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: 30. On renyin Emperor Tianyuan returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 31癸卯，任忠帥步騎七千趣秦郡；

translations.literal: 31. On guimao Ren Zhong led seven thousand foot and horse toward Qin Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: 31. On guimao Ren Zhong led seven thousand foot and horse toward Qin commandery.

sentences.zh: 丙午，仁威將軍魯廣達帥眾入淮；

translations.literal: On bingwu General of Benevolent Prestige Lu Guangda led his troops into the Huai;
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu General of Benevolent Prestige Lu Guangda led his troops into the Huai.

sentences.zh: 是日，樊毅將水軍二萬自東關入焦湖，武毅將軍蕭摩訶帥步騎趣歷陽。

translations.literal: That same day Fan Yi led twenty thousand naval troops from Dongguan into Jiaohu, and General of Martial Prestige Xiao Mohe led foot and horse toward Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Fan Yi led twenty thousand naval troops from Dongguan into Jiaohu, and General of Martial Prestige Xiao Mohe led foot and horse toward Liyang.

sentences.zh: 戊申，韋孝寬拔壽陽，杞公亮拔黃城，梁士彥拔廣陵；

translations.literal: On wushen Wei Xiaokuan took Shouyang, Duke of Qi Liang took Huangcheng, and Liang Shiyan took Guangling;
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Wei Xiaokuan took Shouyang, Duke of Qi Liang took Huangcheng, and Liang Shiyan took Guangling.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，又取霍州。

translations.literal: On xinhai they also took Huozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai they also took Huozhou.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以揚州刺史始興王叔陵為大都督，總水步眾軍。

translations.literal: On guichou Prince Shixing Shuling of Yangzhou was made overall commander to direct all naval and land forces.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Prince Shixing Shuling of Yangzhou was made overall commander of all naval and land forces.

sentences.zh: 32丁巳，周鑄永通萬國錢，一當千，與五行大布並行。

translations.literal: 32. On dingsi Zhou cast Eternal Circulation Ten-Thousand Kingdoms coins, each worth a thousand, to circulate together with the Five Elements large cloth coins.
translations.idiomatic: 32. On dingsi Zhou cast Eternal Circulation Ten-Thousand Kingdoms coins, each worth a thousand, to circulate together with the Five Elements large cloth coins.

sentences.zh: 33十二月，戊午，周天元以災異屢見，捨仗衛，如天興宮。

translations.literal: 33. In the twelfth month, on wuwu, because omens and anomalies had repeatedly appeared, Tianyuan of Zhou laid aside arms and guards and went to Tianxing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: 33. In the twelfth month, on wuwu, because omens and anomalies had repeatedly appeared, Emperor Tianyuan laid aside arms and guards and went to Tianxing Palace.

sentences.zh: 百官上表，勸復寢膳。

translations.literal: The hundred officials submitted memorials urging him to resume normal meals.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred officials submitted memorials urging him to resume normal meals.

sentences.zh: 甲子，還宮，御正武殿，集百官及宮人、外命婦，大列伎樂，初作乞寒胡戲。

translations.literal: On jiazi he returned to the palace, held court at Zhengwu Hall, gathered officials, palace women, and titled ladies from outside, arrayed many musicians and performers, and for the first time staged the begging-cold Hu play.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi he returned to the palace, held court at Zhengwu Hall, gathered officials, palace women, and titled ladies from outside, arrayed many musicians and performers, and for the first time staged the begging-cold Hu play.

sentences.zh: 34乙丑，南、北兗、晉三州及盱眙、山陽、陽平、馬頭、秦、歷陽、沛、北譙、南梁等九郡民並自拔還江南。

translations.literal: 34. On yichou the people of the three prefectures of Southern Yan, Northern Yan, and Jin, and the nine commanderies of Xuyi, Shanyang, Yangping, Matou, Qin, Liyang, Pei, Northern Qiao, and Southern Liang all on their own fled back south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: 34. On yichou the people of Southern Yan, Northern Yan, and Jin prefectures and nine commanderies including Xuyi, Shanyang, Yangping, Matou, Qin, Liyang, Pei, Northern Qiao, and Southern Liang all on their own fled back south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 周又取譙、北徐州。

translations.literal: Zhou also took Qiao and Northern Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou also took Qiao and Northern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 自是江北之地盡沒於周。

translations.literal: From this all territory north of the Yangtze was lost to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: From this all territory north of the Yangtze was lost to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 35周天元如洛陽，親御驛馬，日行三百里，四皇后及文武侍衛數百人並乘馹以從。

translations.literal: 35. Tianyuan of Zhou went to Luoyang, himself drove relay horses, and traveled three hundred li a day; the four empresses and several hundred civil and military attendants all rode post-horses in his train.
translations.idiomatic: 35. Emperor Tianyuan went to Luoyang, drove relay horses himself at three hundred li a day, and the four empresses and several hundred civil and military attendants all rode post-horses in his train.

sentences.zh: 仍令四後方駕齊驅，或有先後，輒加譴責，人馬頓僕，相及於道。

translations.literal: He also ordered the four empresses to drive four-horse teams abreast; if any fell ahead or behind he at once punished them, and men and horses collapsed in exhaustion one after another along the road.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the four empresses to drive four-horse teams abreast; if any fell ahead or behind he punished them at once, and men and horses collapsed in exhaustion one after another along the road.

sentences.zh: 36癸酉，遣平北將軍沈恪、電威將軍裴子烈鎮南徐州，開遠將軍徐道奴鎮柵口，前信州刺史楊寶安鎮白下。

translations.literal: 36. On guiyou he sent Pacifier of the North General Shen Ke, Lightning Prestige General Pei Zilie to garrison Southern Xuzhou, Open Reach General Xu Daonu to garrison Zhakou, and former Governor of Xinzhou Yang Bao'an to garrison Baixia.
translations.idiomatic: 36. On guiyou he sent Pacifier of the North General Shen Ke and Lightning Prestige General Pei Zilie to garrison Southern Xuzhou, Open Reach General Xu Daonu to garrison Zhakou, and former Xinzhou governor Yang Bao'an to garrison Baixia.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以中領軍樊毅都督荊、郢、巴、武四州水陸諸軍事。

translations.literal: On wuyin Central Commander-in-Chief Fan Yi was made commander of all naval and land forces of the four prefectures of Jing, Ying, Ba, and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Central Commander-in-Chief Fan Yi was made commander of all naval and land forces of Jing, Ying, Ba, and Wu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 己卯，周天元還長安。

translations.literal: On jimao Tianyuan of Zhou returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Emperor Tianyuan returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 貞毅將軍汝南周法尚，與長沙王叔堅不相能。

translations.literal: Steadfast Prestige General Zhou Fashang of Runan and Prince Changsha Shujian could not get along.
translations.idiomatic: Steadfast Prestige General Zhou Fashang of Runan and Prince Changsha Shujian could not get along.

sentences.zh: 叔堅譖之於上，雲其欲反。

translations.literal: Shujian slandered him to the emperor, saying he intended rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Shujian slandered him to the emperor, saying he intended rebellion.

sentences.zh: 上執其兄定州刺史法僧，發兵將擊法尚。

translations.literal: The emperor seized his elder brother Faseng, governor of Dingzhou, and sent troops to attack Fashang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor seized his elder brother Faseng, governor of Dingzhou, and sent troops to attack Fashang.

sentences.zh: 法尚奔周，周天元以為開府儀同大將軍、順州刺史，上遣將軍樊猛濟江擊之。

translations.literal: Fashang fled to Zhou; Tianyuan of Zhou made him General of the Open Office with Equal Honor and Governor of Shunzhou; the emperor sent General Fan Meng across the river to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang fled to Zhou; Emperor Tianyuan made him general of the open office with equal honor and governor of Shunzhou; the Chen emperor sent General Fan Meng across the river to attack him.

sentences.zh: 法尚遣部曲督韓朗詐降於猛，曰：「法尚部兵不願降北，人皆竊議，欲叛還。

translations.literal: Fashang sent his troop commander Han Lang to feign surrender to Meng, saying: "Fashang's soldiers do not wish to submit to the north; all secretly discuss returning in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang sent his troop commander Han Lang to feign surrender to Meng, saying, "Fashang's soldiers do not wish to submit to the north; all secretly discuss returning in revolt.

sentences.zh: 若得軍來，自當倒戈。」

translations.literal: If your army comes, they will turn their blades on their own side."
translations.idiomatic: If your army comes, they will turn their blades on their own side."

sentences.zh: 猛以為然，引兵急趨之。

translations.literal: Meng believed him and led his troops in haste toward them.
translations.idiomatic: Meng believed him and led his troops in haste toward them.

sentences.zh: 法尚陽為畏懼，自保江曲，戰而偽走，伏兵邀之。

translations.literal: Fashang pretended fear, held himself along the river bend, fought and feigned flight, and ambush troops intercepted them.
translations.idiomatic: Fashang pretended fear, held the river bend, fought and feigned flight, and ambush troops intercepted them.

sentences.zh: 猛僅以身免，沒者幾八千人。

translations.literal: Meng barely escaped with his life; nearly eight thousand were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Meng barely escaped with his life; nearly eight thousand were lost.
